chapters.title: Chapter 4239 Khor’s Rage! III
paragraphs: In the frozen silence of the Radiant Shore, only a few remained standing.
Noah, his own Quadrillion-level existence a defiant island in the sea of Khor's rage.
Sigrid, her Order a cold, unyielding pillar. The Infiniverse and Ruination, their natures too vast and too alien to be so easily stilled. Malphas!
He floated towards Khor, his expression somber, his voice a calm anchor in her storm.
"Khor. Calm. Tell me what you found."
Her abyssal eyes, now fiery pits of cold, all-devouring hunger, fixed on him.

"These so-called Mutated Inevitabilities," she hissed, her voice a symphony of rage, "have been mutilated. Their Way of Existence altered. They devour and devour endlessly, far beyond what a normal Inevitability would, because they are kept in a cruel, endless state of hunger! They don't even truly eat what they devour! All the Everythings they consume do not stay with them! They are being redirected, stolen, taken elsewhere!"
BOOM!
Noah's frown deepened. The revelation was horrifying.
Khor's voice, though still filled with rage, became a low, dangerous whisper.

"I hold a unique connection to all Inevitabilities. A ruling. The Primacy of Hunger. It grants me a level of control, of understanding. And I can feel it on this... thing. It has been defiled, twisted, used to alter Inevitabilities, to force their very Way of Existence to change. And the only one who had access to my Way of Existence, the only one who could have done this... would be the one who collapsed my existence in the Earliest Folds."
The one who had collapsed her existence.
Noah's expression became even more grave.
Khor's gaze was the most dangerous thing he had ever seen, her eyes radiating a power that promised a terrible, drawn-out end for the one responsible.
"THE Living Paradox...they had better not be Living or Dead," she whispered, her Haki pulsing dangerously.
HUUM!
"Because if they are either..."
In the midst of all this, Noah, his mind a cold engine of logic even in the face of this horror, asked the one question that mattered.
"Where are all the Everythings that Mutated Inevitabilities devour redirected to?"
He felt like he already knew.
Khor went silent. Her rage seemed to cool, to crystallize into something far colder, far more terrifying.
Her voice, when she spoke, was a calm, simple, and utterly devastating whisper.
"THE Loom."
THE Loom!
The words were a final, crushing weight, a capstone on the pyramid of horrors that had been revealed.
The Radiant Shore was frozen in a moment of terrible, absolute silence, a sanctuary held in the grip of Khor's Haki-induced stasis.
Noah stood amidst his unmoving family, the vibrant life of his domain suspended around him like a photograph of a forgotten, happier time.
He looked at Khor, at her tiny form radiating a rage so profound it had stopped time, and he needed to understand.
"How?" he asked, his voice a low, steady current in the dead-still air. "How can you sense this?"
Khor's abyssal eyes, burning with the cold fire of a truth she had just remembered, fixed on him. "I don't just sense it, Outsider," she whispered, the words like grinding glass.
"I feel it still. It is a part of me, a phantom limb that still aches. My Primacy of Hunger, my Way of Existence, my authority over all Inevitabilities... it was mutilated."
She raised a hand, and the very darkness of her Haki seemed to part, revealing a faint, almost invisible network of obsidian threads that stretched out from her and into the void.

"I can feel it, this corrupted version of my own nature. It's a net cast across all of existence, and every Mutated Inevitability is a knot in that net. And all the threads, all the stolen, devoured Everythings they consume... they all flow in one direction."
HUUM!
Her gaze became distant, looking through the fabric of reality itself.

"They lead to a domain lost to existence, a place that is not a place, a fortress built in the heart of nothing. There are doorways that permit only the inflow of this energy, this endless tribute of stolen life. What you all likely know as The Doorways to THE Loom."

Noah's expression became grave, the pieces of a monstrous puzzle clicking into place. As his understanding crystallized, the analytical engine of his own existence responded, its thoughts blooming in his mind as a series of cold, terrible prompts.
Prompts that this time were also displayed to Khor!
|Analysis: The Grand Conspiracy.|
|Primary Hypothesis: The entity known as [THE Living Paradox] is one of the architects of the current existential crisis.|
|Supporting Evidence:|
| - Asset 'Khor' was collapsed by [THE Living Paradox] in the Earliest Folds.|
| - Her unique authority, the [Primacy of Hunger], was not destroyed but stolen and mutilated.|
| - This stolen authority was used to alter the fundamental nature of Inevitabilities, creating the 'Mutated' variant.|

|Conclusion: [THE Living Paradox] has weaponized the very nature of Inevitabilities, transforming them from chaotic predators into a passive, existence-spanning power generation network. Their endless, unsatisfiable hunger is not a flaw; it is the engine. THE Loom is the power station.|
The clinical, professional language of the prompts only served to make the revelation more horrifying.
This was not a natural disaster; it was an act of engineering, a project of unimaginable cruelty and ambition!
|Counter-Strategy Projection: The River of Everythings.|
|Problem: THE Loom is an impenetrable fortress, a one-way system.|
|Analysis: The system is designed for a constant, unidirectional inflow of siphoned Everythings. This creates a conceptual 'current' flowing through all Doorways to THE Loom.|
|Question: Is it possible to reverse this process? Could one, theoretically, 'swim upstream' against this current of devoured Everythings and forcefully enter THE Loom?|
|Success Probability: Unknown, but likely dependent on the ability to manipulate the very authority that created the system in the first place.|
BOOM!

At the thought, Khor's voice, now grave and heavy, cut through the silence. "Such a thing would be insanely difficult, Outsider. The design is only something I can infer right now, but to alter a fundamental flow of existence on that scale... only someone at the Level One Scale of Existence would be able to even attempt it. My old self might have been able to try. But my current self?"
She shook her head, a gesture of profound, bitter frustration.
"It is absolutely impossible. A good deduction, a possibility, but as of right now, and in the near future... impossible."
Her words were a wall, a final, unbreachable barrier of logic. Noah turned silent, the glimmer of a plan extinguished before it could even catch fire.
Khor's eyes, however, flashed with a new, chilling light. Her rage had not dissipated; it had been focused, honed into a sharp, singular purpose.
"I need more information," she declared, her voice a low, dangerous hiss. "I need to enter one of these Doorways to THE Loom."

sentences.text: In the frozen silence of the Radiant Shore, only a few remained standing.
Noah, his own Quadrillion-level existence a defiant island in the sea of Khor's rage.
Sigrid, her Order a cold, unyielding pillar.
The Infiniverse and Ruination, their natures too vast and too alien to be so easily stilled.
Malphas!
He floated towards Khor, his expression somber, his voice a calm anchor in her storm.
"Khor.
Calm.
Tell me what you found."
Her abyssal eyes, now fiery pits of cold, all-devouring hunger, fixed on him.
"These so-called Mutated Inevitabilities," she hissed, her voice a symphony of rage, "have been mutilated.
Their Way of Existence altered.
They devour and devour endlessly, far beyond what a normal Inevitability would, because they are kept in a cruel, endless state of hunger!
They don't even truly eat what they devour!
All the Everythings they consume do not stay with them!
They are being redirected, stolen, taken elsewhere!"
BOOM!
Noah's frown deepened.
The revelation was horrifying.
Khor's voice, though still filled with rage, became a low, dangerous whisper.
"I hold a unique connection to all Inevitabilities.
A ruling.
The Primacy of Hunger.
It grants me a level of control, of understanding.
And I can feel it on this... thing.
It has been defiled, twisted, used to alter Inevitabilities, to force their very Way of Existence to change.
And the only one who had access to my Way of Existence, the only one who could have done this... would be the one who collapsed my existence in the Earliest Folds."
The one who had collapsed her existence.
Noah's expression became even more grave.
Khor's gaze was the most dangerous thing he had ever seen, her eyes radiating a power that promised a terrible, drawn-out end for the one responsible.
"THE Living Paradox...they had better not be Living or Dead," she whispered, her Haki pulsing dangerously.
HUUM!
"Because if they are either..."
In the midst of all this, Noah, his mind a cold engine of logic even in the face of this horror, asked the one question that mattered.
"Where are all the Everythings that Mutated Inevitabilities devour redirected to?"
He felt like he already knew.
Khor went silent.
Her rage seemed to cool, to crystallize into something far colder, far more terrifying.
Her voice, when she spoke, was a calm, simple, and utterly devastating whisper.
"THE Loom."
THE Loom!
The words were a final, crushing weight, a capstone on the pyramid of horrors that had been revealed.
The Radiant Shore was frozen in a moment of terrible, absolute silence, a sanctuary held in the grip of Khor's Haki-induced stasis.
Noah stood amidst his unmoving family, the vibrant life of his domain suspended around him like a photograph of a forgotten, happier time.
He looked at Khor, at her tiny form radiating a rage so profound it had stopped time, and he needed to understand.
"How?" he asked, his voice a low, steady current in the dead-still air.
"How can you sense this?"
Khor's abyssal eyes, burning with the cold fire of a truth she had just remembered, fixed on him.
"I don't just sense it, Outsider," she whispered, the words like grinding glass.
"I feel it still.
It is a part of me, a phantom limb that still aches.
My Primacy of Hunger, my Way of Existence, my authority over all Inevitabilities... it was mutilated."
She raised a hand, and the very darkness of her Haki seemed to part, revealing a faint, almost invisible network of obsidian threads that stretched out from her and into the void.
"I can feel it, this corrupted version of my own nature.
It's a net cast across all of existence, and every Mutated Inevitability is a knot in that net.
And all the threads, all the stolen, devoured Everythings they consume... they all flow in one direction."
HUUM!
Her gaze became distant, looking through the fabric of reality itself.
"They lead to a domain lost to existence, a place that is not a place, a fortress built in the heart of nothing.
There are doorways that permit only the inflow of this energy, this endless tribute of stolen life.
What you all likely know as The Doorways to THE Loom."
Noah's expression became grave, the pieces of a monstrous puzzle clicking into place.
As his understanding crystallized, the analytical engine of his own existence responded, its thoughts blooming in his mind as a series of cold, terrible prompts.
Prompts that this time were also displayed to Khor!

chapters.title: Chapter 4240 End! I
paragraphs: At her words, Noah's pondering gaze shifted. He reached into the impossible space of his own existence, and he took out... a key.
It was a simple, gray rectangular object, almost mundane in its appearance. A Key. The Frequency of Existence that had once been Hell Terra Firma!
It needed an influx of paradoxical authority to activate, and now, in this Shore, it shone with a faint, expectant light.
"I have a Key to a Doorway to THE Loom," he said, his voice a quiet statement.
Khor's eyes widened, a flicker of genuine surprise in her ancient gaze. "How did you get your hands on something like that?"

Noah's gaze drifted to the frozen figures of Bob and the Mutated Inevitability. "In my home Wheel of Existence, this Key used to be in the form of a mere Frequency of Existence. Actually... Little Bobby and others were looking for it. He was doing everything he could to find a path to bring back his daughter. But after everything was over and done, I obtained this Key. And now..."
His eyes flashed with a sharp, almost cruel, light as he thought of the intricate, looping patterns of existence.

A cold smile touched his lips. "Isn't it unique how cause and effect works? From all those events back then, and how they led to Thauron, who initially had this Inevitability, which in turn led to my first meetings with Living Existences... Now Bob comes back, holding a Mutated Inevitability he fears, which allows you to see the horror of it all. And now, the Key, from all the way back then, is in play again. Existence...seems to be intricately unique."
Khor nodded, her expression cold.

"Choices, Outsider," she said, her voice a low murmur. "They steer one's weavings of existence. In the vast unfairness of it all, only the choices one makes truly matter, for they are the only rudder you have. Without choices, you would only be pulled into the Flow and Weavings of others."
She looked at him, at the impossible being he was, at the frozen court of powerful entities that now surrounded him.
"You... seem to have pulled Living Existences, me, and many others into your Weavings. Continue to make your choices, Outsider."
Her gaze fell upon the Key in his hand, her eyes burning with a new, focused intensity.
"For now, let's see what we can find from the Doorway that Key leads into."
The heavy, frozen silence of the Radiant Shore began to thaw.
One by one, the beings suspended in the grip of Khor's Haki stirred, their consciousnesses slowly returning to their forms like a tide creeping back up a silent beach as Khor's Haki began to recede.
Noah stood amidst them, his presence a calm, unshakable anchor in their sea of confusion.
He looked at Khor, who was now calmly observing the still-unconscious form of Bob and the writhing, contained Mutated Inevitability.
Her rage had subsided, replaced by a cold, analytical focus.
"Let's see what we can find," she had repeated. It was time to open the door.

Noah's gaze settled on the gray, rectangular object in his hand. The Key. A relic from his own past, a piece of a forgotten story that had, through the intricate, looping weavings of existence, become the key to his future.
It pulsed with a faint, expectant light, awakened by the chaotic, paradoxical energies that now saturated his Shore. He had already filled it to the brim and activated it!
He tossed it into the air.
It hung there for a moment, a simple, mundane object in a realm of impossible beauty.
Then, Noah channeled his will. A stream of pure, paradoxical authority shot from his hand and into the Key for a final push.

It began to spin. A heavy, resonant hum filled the air, the sound of an ancient lock finding its long-lost key. Paradoxical waves of gray and silver light pulsed outward, distorting the very air, making the golden sands seem to ripple and flow like water. Where the light passed, reality seemed to thin, to become more... suggestive.
In moments, a massive, rectangular gray portal, a perfect, clean-edged wound in the fabric of the Shore, began to form!
|[Key to Doorway #9384] has been activated.|
|Analysis: The influx of high-grade paradoxical authority has optimized the activation sequence. A stable, permanent pathway is being established.|
|Process: The pathway is aligning itself with the unique weavings of the Radiant Shore, creating a synergistic connection that will reinforce both the portal and the Shore itself.|
|Conclusion: A Permanent Portal to Doorway #9384 of THE Loom has been established. You may now enter and exit at your leisure. |
The portal solidified, its gray, shimmering surface a silent, waiting invitation. Noah and Khor stood before it. In her abyssal eyes, a chilling, predatory light had begun to burn.
Noah looked at her, at the barely contained fury that still simmered beneath her calm exterior, and he spoke, his voice a gentle reminder. "Khor. Your Haki."

A flicker of something...surprise, then a hint of apologetic light, flashed in her eyes. The immense, oppressive pressure that had settled over the Shore in the wake of her rage finally, completely, released.
"Sorry about that, Outsider," she said, her voice returning to its usual, melodic cadence. "A percentage of my power leaked out due to my anger. It shouldn't cause any long-lasting effects."
A percentage. Noah smiled calmly at the terrifying understatement.
In his Shore, his people awoke with a collective, shuddering gasp, the memory of that all-consuming, absolute darkness still fresh in their minds.
He glanced at his conceptual screen, at the chaos unfolding outside the Aegis, and wondered just how that 'leak' would change the game he had set in motion.
A clone, a perfect duplicate of himself, emerged from his body. A similar phenomenon occurred with Khor, her own miniature copy stepping forth from her shadow.
Noah called out, "Malphas."
The Attendant appeared in a whisper of respectful silence. He bowed.
The three of them, the clones of the Tyrant and the Hunger, and the ever-faithful servant, turned and stepped into the gray, shimmering veil of the portal!

chapters.title: Chapter 4241 End! II
paragraphs: The main body of Noah remained on the Shore, watching as his people, groggy and disoriented, began to wake.

The main body of Khor, her task here not yet finished, floated towards the now-conscious form of Bob and the still-writhing Mutated Inevitability, her expression a mixture of clinical curiosity and ancient sorrow.
Outside, in the region of Collapse, the three Dukes of Law who had remained awake were reeling.
The avalanche of darkness that had washed over them from the Aegis had been a force beyond their comprehension. It had not been an attack, but a simple, absolute statement of power!
"What... was that?" Duke Themis whispered, her voice, usually so steady, trembling with a profound, existential dread.
The Early Tools they wore, artifacts of immense power, still glowed with a protective, legalistic light, the only reason their consciousnesses hadn't been snuffed out like all the others.
As they were finishing their panicked discussion, a new wave of arrivals began.
Portals of every color and authority ripped open across the void.
Living Origins, Living Elementals, Living Quantums... even more Living Paradoxes, their Marks of Unity shining like defiant stars, poured into the region, their numbers in the hundreds.
A certain butler had been busy!
A contingent of Origin Dukes, led by a clone of Origin Ama Gias herself, appeared near the Laws.
"What happened here? We heard of The Sanctuary of THE Creature?" Gias demanded, her gaze sweeping over the hundreds of unconscious Living Laws that were only now beginning to stir.
Duke Justinius, his symmetrical form radiating a tense, controlled fury, simply replied, "Not everything here is as it appears."
Of those who heard this cryptic exchange, one did not have the patience for subtlety.
A fiery Living Elemental Duke, his body a raging inferno of molten rock and solar flares, shot towards the blue-gold Aegis.
"Enough of this waiting! If it truly has any connections with THE Creature or THE Living Existences...hmph!" he roared.
With a bellow that could have shattered Wheels, he breathed out a terrifying pillar of pure, conceptual flame that smashed onto the barrier.

The Aegis hummed, absorbing the attack. And then, at the point of impact, it leaked. A few radiant Sacred Herbs and a shower of shimmering, Early Sacred Water droplets erupted from the barrier, a reward for the Duke's fiery impatience!
He caught them, his eyes widening in shock and then blazing with a raw, covetous light. He turned to the Living Laws. "Is this what you have been hiding?!"
Before they could explain, it was too late. The scent of the treasure, the very idea of it, had spread.
The phase of greed had arrived.

Dukes, Honored Existences, and Royals from every faction arrived in a slow yet quick pace, their caution consumed by the promise of impossible loot, began to surround the Aegis as first, they sought to understand.
Then, they attacked after they heard the reports from what was currently known!
And with every strike, more herbs, more sacred water, more priceless treasures rained down.
It was a glorious, chaotic honey pot!
The Living Laws, seeing the other factions reaping a bounty from a fortress they had discovered, gritted their teeth.
Their pride and their greed warred, and greed won. They too joined the assault, their own authorities of law now used to batter the very thing they had been trying to analyze.
Justinius, remembering the terrifying burst of power he had barely survived, simply advised his forces to keep their distance as they attacked!
He shook his head as he watched the fervany scene.
Back inside the Radiant Shore, Noah stood on the golden sands near the gray portal, a devilish smile on his face as he watched the frenzy unfold.
|[Architect's Rebuke] is in continuous activation.|
|The Honey Pot Protocol is a resounding success. Multiple high-level entities are now willingly feeding your fortress. It's like they're paying you to rob them.|
|Siphoning Hostile Authority: [Living Law], [Living Origin], [Living Elemental], [Living Quantum]...|
|A diverse portfolio of existential energies is being collected.|
|Defensive Engrams are being created at an unprecedented rate.|
|Incoming Complexity and Purity being siphoned into the Engram: +17 Trillion...+30 Trillion...+40 Trillion...|
|Current Status: You are now actively profiting from a multi-faction siege on your own home. This is a new benchmark in tyrannical efficiency.|
Noah watched these flashing prompts as his other body and the clones of Khor and Malphas passed through the veil, and the existence dissolved.

They appeared in a realm of gray, muted brilliance. All around them, massive, craggy rocks that looked like shattered meteors floated in a silent, empty void, each one connected to its neighbors by thick, archaic gray chains. It was a graveyard of existence, a prison of forgotten matter.
|Due to the presence of Khor, The First Hunger, the passage through Doorway #9384 of THE Loom has bypassed all intermediary zones.|
|You have arrived at the endpoint. This is the closest any being can potentially come to the periphery of THE Loom.|
HUUM!
Due to Khor... they had cheated the journey itself, arriving directly at the end!
And it was an end. The moment they fully materialized, they saw it.
Far ahead, and all around, stretching into the infinite gray distance, were thousands upon thousands of Mutated Inevitabilities.
They were arranged like a great, silent swarm, their writhing, tentacled forms a sea of ceaseless, hungry motion.
And from each of them, a single, shimmering tendril of pure, siphoned essence floated out, all of them leading to... a single, stellar gray object.
It was a receiver, a nexus. It looked like a colossal, multifaceted crystal, its surface constantly shifting, its form both geometric and organic.
It radiated a terrifying light of pure, unadulterated complexity, and it was attached to a massive, endlessly expanding gray well, a vortex of pure energy surrounded by pulsing, circular gray rings.
It was here. This was where all the devoured Everythings of the Inevitabilities here were flowing into!
Khor's form trembled, a low, guttural growl of pure, bubbling rage and pain escaping her.
Malphas became stern, stepping forward to stand protectively in front of Noah. In the next moment, the thousands of Mutated Inevitabilities turned their countless, vacant eyes towards them.
A collective, soul-shattering screech echoed through the void, and they charged.

The weakest among them held 100 Trillion in Complexity. The strongest, great, leviathan-like beings at the heart of the swarm, exceeded 100 Quadrillion. They were a tide of absolute, unmakeable power.
Khor looked at them, and her rage was tempered by a profound, heartbreaking sorrow.
They were her children, her kin, and they did not even recognize their Mother.

"See if you can learn anything from that object, maybe the idea of your weavings to follow where the Everythings flow to may have a chance if we understand that," she said to Noah, her voice a tight, strained whisper.
"I will hold them back. I will give you enough time."
Noah nodded, his eyes shining. He and Malphas shot forward, not away from the onslaught, but towards it, towards the nexus.
With a single thought, Noah wove the Artifice of Quantum, and with a single step, he was no longer there, but here, directly before the stellar gray object.
The thousands of Inevitabilities instantly shifted their trajectory, their eyes blazing with a furious red light as they turned their full, annihilating attention on him!
But at that moment, Khor's voice, now filled with a deep, melancholic power, echoed out.
"You poor things," she said. "Existence has been so cruel to you. Listen to Mother... and hold still."
Listen to Mother!
Hold still!
BOOM!
A unique, invisible authority of hunger erupted from her.
In an instant, the thousands of charging Inevitabilities, their tentacles just inches from Noah, froze.
They were held in perfect, absolute stasis, their own natures forcing them to obey the will of The First Hunger, even as their mutilated forms compelled them to protect the object they served.
Noah's eyes were luminous.
Behind him, Malphas appeared, a silent, crimson-eyed guardian.

Noah was on the cusp of answers. Was this object truly the nexus for this Doorway? The collection point for all stolen Everythings? Did all the Doorways to THE Loom that Living Existences had been traversing over the eons...all hold an end like this that they could not reach because Inevitabilities with Complexities even exceeding Early Creatures appeared towards the end?
He had to know!
His figure became wrapped in brilliant, bloody purple flames, his Heart of an Early Creature pulsing with a furious, tyrannical rhythm.
He reached out, his hand about to touch the stellar gray object, and he bellowed, his voice a command to Existence itself!
"Give the Everythings you have swallowed... TO ME!"
A terrifying, gray light erupted from the object, a defensive pulse that washed over him.
But he pushed through, his hand making contact. He felt it...an immense, infinite well of weavings of complexity and purity.
|You have come into contact with a Primordial Lodestone of THE Loom.|
|This object serves as a collection and transference node for siphoned Everythings of a small section of Existence passed through a single Doorway.|
|It currently contains countless Everythings that have not yet been harvested and absorbed.|
Noah's eyes blazed with a fervent light.
"Give them all to me" he bellowed with a profound sense of Tyranny!
|Attempting to extract the Everythings from the Lodestone...|
|Attempting to extract...|
HUUM!
But then, it happened.
A blinding, gray light, heavier and more absolute than the one before, erupted.
The Lodestone flashed with a deep, crimson light. As if something had gone wrong, and a failsafe had been triggered!
His entire existence buzzed, and a terrifying, unknown force erupted from the Lodestone, clamping onto his hands, holding them in place.
A torrent of alien, corrupting authority began to gush from the Lodestone and into his body right after as he felt like snakes were penetrating into his skin!
|ERROR. ERROR. UNKNOWN FAILSAFE TRIGGERED.|
|THE AUTHORITY OF THE LODESTONE HAS BEEN ALTERED.|
|YOUR EXISTENCE IS BEING CORRUPTED!|
Noah's eyes flashed with a mixture of Tyranny and rage as he tried to pull back, but he was held fast.
"My Lord!" Malphas cried, turning in shock and surging forward to pull his master away.
"Outsider!" Khor's expression changed to one of pure alarm. She took a step, appearing right beside Noah, her hand reaching for him!
But it was too late.

|An undeniable weaving of Existence, far exceeding anything currently experienced, is attacking and corrupting the very makeup of your being. All of your being across all possible bodies, weavings, and timelines.|
|The entirety of your existence rises up in defense. Your Heart, your Atlas, your Principles, your very Will, your Everythings... they are fighting back.|
|Your Systems of Existence are attempting to counteract the rewriting of your fundamental Code of Existence by the Corruption of the Lodestone.|
|Counter-measures failing...|
|Existential Integrity dropping...|
|Error. Error. Error!|
THUMP!
Noah's eyes pulsed.
He stopped feeling all sensation.
He only felt the beat of his heart.
His glorious Heart.
THUMP!
|Error.|
Thump!
|Error.|
The beat was getting fainter.
And fainter.
Thump.
|Erro-|
In Noah's eyes, across all his bodies, in the Radiant Shore, in the Wandering Territories, in the deepest corridors of his own Existence...
Everything went dark.
Everything.
Everything... but a faint blue light of the most recently crafted Seed Glyph.

sentences.text: The main body of Noah remained on the Shore, watching as his people, groggy and disoriented, began to wake.

The main body of Khor, her task here not yet finished, floated towards the now-conscious form of Bob and the still-writhing Mutated Inevitability, her expression a mixture of clinical curiosity and ancient sorrow.
Outside, in the region of Collapse, the three Dukes of Law who had remained awake were reeling.
The avalanche of darkness that had washed over them from the Aegis had been a force beyond their comprehension.
It had not been an attack, but a simple, absolute statement of power!
"What... was that?" Duke Themis whispered, her voice, usually so steady, trembling with a profound, existential dread.
The Early Tools they wore, artifacts of immense power, still glowed with a protective, legalistic light, the only reason their consciousnesses hadn't been snuffed out like all the others.
As they were finishing their panicked discussion, a new wave of arrivals began.
Portals of every color and authority ripped open across the void.
Living Origins, Living Elementals, Living Quantums... even more Living Paradoxes, their Marks of Unity shining like defiant stars, poured into the region, their numbers in the hundreds.
A certain butler had been busy!
A contingent of Origin Dukes, led by a clone of Origin Ama Gias herself, appeared near the Laws.
"What happened here?
We heard of The Sanctuary of THE Creature?" Gias demanded, her gaze sweeping over the hundreds of unconscious Living Laws that were only now beginning to stir.
Duke Justinius, his symmetrical form radiating a tense, controlled fury, simply replied, "Not everything here is as it appears."
Of those who heard this cryptic exchange, one did not have the patience for subtlety.
A fiery Living Elemental Duke, his body a raging inferno of molten rock and solar flares, shot towards the blue-gold Aegis.
"Enough of this waiting!
If it truly has any connections with THE Creature or THE Living Existences...hmph!" he roared.
With a bellow that could have shattered Wheels, he breathed out a terrifying pillar of pure, conceptual flame that smashed onto the barrier.
The Aegis hummed, absorbing the attack.
And then, at the point of impact, it leaked.
A few radiant Sacred Herbs and a shower of shimmering, Early Sacred Water droplets erupted from the barrier, a reward for the Duke's fiery impatience!
He caught them, his eyes widening in shock and then blazing with a raw, covetous light.
He turned to the Living Laws.
"Is this what you have been hiding?!"
Before they could explain, it was too late.
The scent of the treasure, the very idea of it, had spread.
The phase of greed had arrived.

Dukes, Honored Existences, and Royals from every faction arrived in a slow yet quick pace, their caution consumed by the promise of impossible loot, began to surround the Aegis as first, they sought to understand.
Then, they attacked after they heard the reports from what was currently known!
And with every strike, more herbs, more sacred water, more priceless treasures rained down.
It was a glorious, chaotic honey pot!
The Living Laws, seeing the other factions reaping a bounty from a fortress they had discovered, gritted their teeth.
Their pride and their greed warred, and greed won.
They too joined the assault, their own authorities of law now used to batter the very thing they had been trying to analyze.
Justinius, remembering the terrifying burst of power he had barely survived, simply advised his forces to keep their distance as they attacked!
He shook his head as he watched the fervany scene.
Back inside the Radiant Shore, Noah stood on the golden sands near the gray portal, a devilish smile on his face as he watched the frenzy unfold.
|[Architect's Rebuke] is in continuous activation.|
|The Honey Pot Protocol is a resounding success.
Multiple high-level entities are now willingly feeding your fortress.
It's like they're paying you to rob them.|
|Siphoning Hostile Authority: [Living Law], [Living Origin], [Living Elemental], [Living Quantum]...|
|A diverse portfolio of existential energies is being collected.|
|Defensive Engrams are being created at an unprecedented rate.|
|Incoming Complexity and Purity being siphoned into the Engram: +17 Trillion...+30 Trillion...+40 Trillion...|
|Current Status: You are now actively profiting from a multi-faction siege on your own home.
This is a new benchmark in tyrannical efficiency.|
Noah watched these flashing prompts as his other body and the clones of Khor and Malphas passed through the veil, and the existence dissolved.
They appeared in a realm of gray, muted brilliance.
All around them, massive, craggy rocks that looked like shattered meteors floated in a silent, empty void, each one connected to its neighbors by thick, archaic gray chains.
It was a graveyard of existence, a prison of forgotten matter.
|Due to the presence of Khor, The First Hunger, the passage through Doorway #9384 of THE Loom has bypassed all intermediary zones.|
|You have arrived at the endpoint.
This is the closest any being can potentially come to the periphery of THE Loom.|
HUUM!
Due to Khor... they had cheated the journey itself, arriving directly at the end!
And it was an end.
The moment they fully materialized, they saw it.
Far ahead, and all around, stretching into the infinite gray distance, were thousands upon thousands of Mutated Inevitabilities.
They were arranged like a great, silent swarm, their writhing, tentacled forms a sea of ceaseless, hungry motion.
And from each of them, a single, shimmering tendril of pure, siphoned essence floated out, all of them leading to... a single, stellar gray object.
It was a receiver, a nexus.
It looked like a colossal, multifaceted crystal, its surface constantly shifting, its form both geometric and organic.
It radiated a terrifying light of pure, unadulterated complexity, and it was attached to a massive, endlessly expanding gray well, a vortex of pure energy surrounded by pulsing, circular gray rings.
It was here.
This was where all the devoured Everythings of the Inevitabilities here were flowing into!
Khor's form trembled, a low, guttural growl of pure, bubbling rage and pain escaping her.
Malphas became stern, stepping forward to stand protectively in front of Noah.
In the next moment, the thousands of Mutated Inevitabilities turned their countless, vacant eyes towards them.
A collective, soul-shattering screech echoed through the void, and they charged.
The weakest among them held 100 Trillion in Complexity.
The strongest, great, leviathan-like beings at the heart of the swarm, exceeded 100 Quadrillion.
They were a tide of absolute, unmakeable power.
Khor looked at them, and her rage was tempered by a profound, heartbreaking sorrow.
They were her children, her kin, and they did not even recognize their Mother.

"See if you can learn anything from that object, maybe the idea of your weavings to follow where the Everythings flow to may have a chance if we understand that," she said to Noah, her voice a tight, strained whisper.
"I will hold them back.
I will give you enough time."
Noah nodded, his eyes shining.
He and Malphas shot forward, not away from the onslaught, but towards it, towards the nexus.
With a single thought, Noah wove the Artifice of Quantum, and with a single step, he was no longer there, but here, directly before the stellar gray object.
The thousands of Inevitabilities instantly shifted their trajectory, their eyes blazing with a furious red light as they turned their full, annihilating attention on him!
But at that moment, Khor's voice, now filled with a deep, melancholic power, echoed out.
"You poor things," she said.
"Existence has been so cruel to you.
Listen to Mother... and hold still."
Listen to Mother!
Hold still!
BOOM!
A unique, invisible authority of hunger erupted from her.
In an instant, the thousands of charging Inevitabilities, their tentacles just inches from Noah, froze.
They were held in perfect, absolute stasis, their own natures forcing them to obey the will of The First Hunger, even as their mutilated forms compelled them to protect the object they served.
Noah's eyes were luminous.
Behind him, Malphas appeared, a silent, crimson-eyed guardian.
Noah was on the cusp of answers.
Was this object truly the nexus for this Doorway?
The collection point for all stolen Everythings?

Did all the Doorways to THE Loom that Living Existences had been traversing over the eons...all hold an end like this that they could not reach because Inevitabilities with Complexities even exceeding Early Creatures appeared towards the end?
He had to know!
His figure became wrapped in brilliant, bloody purple flames, his Heart of an Early Creature pulsing with a furious, tyrannical rhythm.
He reached out, his hand about to touch the stellar gray object, and he bellowed, his voice a command to Existence itself!
"Give the Everythings you have swallowed...
TO ME!"
A terrifying, gray light erupted from the object, a defensive pulse that washed over him.
But he pushed through, his hand making contact.
He felt it...an immense, infinite well of weavings of complexity and purity.
|You have come into contact with a Primordial Lodestone of THE Loom.|
|This object serves as a collection and transference node for siphoned Everythings of a small section of Existence passed through a single Doorway.|
|It currently contains countless Everythings that have not yet been harvested and absorbed.|
Noah's eyes blazed with a fervent light.
"Give them all to me" he bellowed with a profound sense of Tyranny!
|Attempting to extract the Everythings from the Lodestone...|
|Attempting to extract...|
HUUM!
But then, it happened.
A blinding, gray light, heavier and more absolute than the one before, erupted.
The Lodestone flashed with a deep, crimson light.
As if something had gone wrong, and a failsafe had been triggered!
His entire existence buzzed, and a terrifying, unknown force erupted from the Lodestone, clamping onto his hands, holding them in place.
A torrent of alien, corrupting authority began to gush from the Lodestone and into his body right after as he felt like snakes were penetrating into his skin!
|ERROR.
ERROR.
UNKNOWN FAILSAFE TRIGGERED.|
|THE AUTHORITY OF THE LODESTONE HAS BEEN ALTERED.|
|YOUR EXISTENCE IS BEING CORRUPTED!|
Noah's eyes flashed with a mixture of Tyranny and rage as he tried to pull back, but he was held fast.
"My Lord!" Malphas cried, turning in shock and surging forward to pull his master away.
"Outsider!" Khor's expression changed to one of pure alarm.
She took a step, appearing right beside Noah, her hand reaching for him!
But it was too late.
|An undeniable weaving of Existence, far exceeding anything currently experienced, is attacking and corrupting the very makeup of your being.
All of your being across all possible bodies, weavings, and timelines.|
|The entirety of your existence rises up in defense.
Your Heart, your Atlas, your Principles, your very Will, your Everythings... they are fighting back.|
|Your Systems of Existence are attempting to counteract the rewriting of your fundamental Code of Existence by the Corruption of the Lodestone.|
|Counter-measures failing...|
|Existential Integrity dropping...|
|Error.
Error.
Error!|
THUMP!
Noah's eyes pulsed.
He stopped feeling all sensation.
He only felt the beat of his heart.
His glorious Heart.
THUMP!
|Error.|
Thump!
|Error.|
The beat was getting fainter.
And fainter.
Thump.
|Erro-|
In Noah's eyes, across all his bodies, in the Radiant Shore, in the Wandering Territories, in the deepest corridors of his own Existence...
Everything went dark.
Everything.
Everything... but a faint blue light of the most recently crafted Seed Glyph.

chapters.title: Chapter 4242 The Loom I
paragraphs: When skies crack wide and Veils grow thin,
When Dead and Living merge as kin,
When Folds collapse to crushing dark,
The Loom preserves the chosen spark.
First comes the thinning of The Veil,
The Dead arise where Living fail,
Then tears appear in reality's seam,
As nightmares walk and dreamers scream.
THE Creature's works shall turn to dust,
Early powers break like rust,
Quadrillions, Quintillions fall to null and void,
As Everythings are all destroyed.
But we who dwell within the Frame,
We who know the Weaver's name,
We who paid the price to enter,
Stand secure in Loom's great center.
For when the Fallout comes to call,
And Civilizational falls to thrall,
When Zero Scale meets final rest,
The Loom alone shall stand the test.
No Hunger's jaw can breach our wall,
The Loom protects us from the Fall.
Count your fortune, chosen few,
Selected from the countless who,
Will face the ending unprepared,
While we within The Loom are spared.
Remember those who built this ark,
Who saw the coming of the dark,
THE Living Paradox who knew,
What none outside could misconstrue.
So when you hear the outside cry,
When trillions beg before they die,
Remember that you earned your place,
Within The Loom's protecting grace.
For Existence ends beyond these walls,
The mighty crash, the lowest falls,
But we shall wait in patient power,
Until arrives the Blooming Hour.
When Fallout fades and birth begins,
When those inside The Loom step in,
To fill the void that ending made,
As architects of the next parade.
This is the promise, this the creed,
The Loom provides for those in need,
Who saw the truth and chose to hide,
Rather than face the coming tide.
Let others call us cowards, weak,
Let them their hopeless glory seek,
We know the truth that they deny:
Outside The Loom, all things must die.
All for the sake of Civilization.
All for the sake of Civilization.
All for the sake of Civilization.
All for the sake of Civilization.
<THE Loom, Unknown Location>
The room was a sanctuary of quiet, stellar brilliance.

The walls were not carved from stone or metal, but forged from a white, sparkling wood that hummed with a life of its own, a material that had been common in the Earliest Folds but was now a forgotten myth.
The air was still, clean, and saturated with a power so pure and so dense that breathing was a form of cultivation!
Breathing here alone would have the same effects as devouring Sacred Herbs.
The only object in the vast, empty space was a single crimson mat, its fabric woven from threads of solidified authority.

It was an Early Tool, and it radiated a unique, gentle warmth, a passive aura that increased the complexity and purity of any being who rested upon it by millions every second- up until a certain threshold anyways!
Upon this mat, a figure stretched with a languid, feline grace.
It was a woman...an Early Creature, her form a perfect testament to a forgotten age of primordial power!
Her hair was a cascade of vibrant, fiery red, each strand a filament of captured starlight that seemed to move with its own will.

She yawned, a delicate, soundless gesture, and as she did, her power pulsed, a wave of complexity and purity so immense it made the very fabric of the room ripple. It was a power that overwhelmingly exceeded 2000 Quadrillion, a number so vast it had lost all meaning, becoming simply a statement of absolute, undeniable might.
And mighty she was!
She rose, and the simple crimson robe she wore shimmered. On the left breast, the marking of a single, golden flame burned with a gentle, contained fire.
She walked out of the room, her bare feet silent on the polished, white-wood floors.

She entered a hall that seemed to stretch into infinity, forged from the same living material, its pristine white walls lined with intricate, crimson-gold etchings that depicted the birth of folds and the forging of concepts.
The moment she emerged, a being of living, swirling frost glided past.
It was a Living Elemental, its form a beautiful, terrible blizzard contained in a vaguely humanoid shape.
It smiled, a gesture that caused the air around it to sparkle with ice crystals. "Esteemed Valkyrie," its voice was the sound of a winter wind whispering through ancient trees.
"We are holding an Elemental Crucible today. A small tournament, a test of skill. Only Early Creatures and Elementals below 500 Quadrillion are permitted to participate. Will you be coming?"

Valkyrie shook her head, a gentle, warm smile on her lips. The Living Elemental before her emanated waves of power at a staggering 150 Quadrillion, yet in this place, it was considered a participant for a junior tournament!
"No," she said, her voice a soft, melodic hum. "You all enjoy yourselves."
She continued her path down the grand hall, her presence a silent, respected authority.
She passed other Early Creatures, their forms ranging from the perfectly humanoid to the beautifully abstract.
She passed other Living Elementals...a being of living, shifting earth whose very presence had the gravity of a Folds; another of pure, sentient fire whose warmth was a comforting balm.
Each of them, Early Creature and Living Elemental alike, held a power that exceeded 100 Quadrillion at the very least.
And as she passed, each of them would offer a silent nod, a gesture of profound respect.
Ultimately, she came to a massive door at the end of the hall, a gate that opened with a silent, willing parting of reality itself.
She stepped through into a space so vast it defied comprehension.
It was a forest of light and power, a garden that stretched for countless light-years. Massive, radiant trees, each one the size of a galaxy, pulsed with the raw, untamed energy of the elements.
One tree was a pillar of living fire, its leaves solar flares. Another was a colossal glacier, its branches carved from ice that was older than time.
Tens of thousands of Living Elementals and hundreds of auras of Early Creatures could be felt, moving like fireflies in this impossible, cosmic arboretum!
A calm, disembodied voice echoed through the space, a sound that was both everywhere and nowhere at once.
"Welcome to the Arboretum Primus, Commander Valkyrie."

chapters.title: Chapter 4243 The Loom II
paragraphs: Valkyrie smiled and nodded, her form lifting from the ground as she floated towards the very center of this light-year-wide expanse.
There, nine massive crimson thrones, each carved from a single, solidified concept of command, were arranged in a circle.
From each throne, crimson-gold lines of pure, informational light shot out, connecting to the myriad of massive, elemental trees.
She drifted towards one of the empty thrones, her gaze sweeping over the other eight Early Creatures who were already seated.
Some were lost in deep cultivation, the faint, shimmering light of one or even multiple Principles surrounding them like halos of impossible power.
Each of them, like her, wore a crimson robe, and each of them radiated a power that was well in excess of 2000 Quadrillion!
"Any changes today?" she asked, her voice a quiet question to the empty air.
The same disembodied, monotone voice replied.
"No, Commander. Just like all the eons before. No changes."
Valkyrie hummed and nodded, a familiar, almost weary, ritual. She settled into her throne, and as she did, illusory crimson-gold screens rose before her, displaying a cascade of information.
She scanned the data, her eyes taking in the endless stream of reports. Everything was green. Every system was nominal. Every projection was stable.
"Give me the daily report," she said.

"Daily Report: Everythings harvested in the last cycle: 1.9 Million Units. All monitored zones continue to be oversaturated with a surplus of Everythings. Distribution protocols are operating at 30% capacity to avoid systemic overload."
Valkyrie nodded with a faint, satisfied smile.
The system worked. The great engine they had built was not just stable; it was overwhelmingly successful. But at this moment, shockingly...
BZZT!
An alarm!
A shrill, discordant sound that had no place in this realm of perfect, unchanging order.

It was a sound none of them had heard in their lifetimes. Valkyrie and the other eight Commanders were jolted from their serene contemplation, their eyes snapping open, their expressions a mixture of confusion and dawning alarm.
Valkyrie's hands flew across her screens, her fingers a blur as she pulled up the system overview.
It was a vast, holographic chart showing hundreds of glowing green nodes of light.
And there, in a distant, almost forgotten sector, was one node that was not green. It was cracked, and it was shining with a frantic, angry red.

Her eyes widened in genuine surprise. "It seems," she murmured, her voice a low, disbelieving whisper, "something managed to get near a Lodestone and even interrupt its functions. Its Corruption of Collapse has already been triggered..."
The other Commanders were stirring, their calm facades cracking. "This...has not happened before, has it?" one of them commented, his voice a low rumble.

Another nodded, his form a shimmering mirage of heat and power. "No. When such a thing occurs, the protocol is to let those above us know and to initiate the Closure Protocols. We begin closing the Doorways designated for us to monitor. We have collections of hundreds of times the Everythings we expected, anyway. Far exceeding any parameters."
Valkyrie nodded, a strange, melancholic sadness in her eyes. "I will pass the word on. It is just... sad."
A burly, muscular Early Creature, seated on a throne to her right laughed with a harsh, grating sound.

"Why is it sad, Valkyrie? Because the existence who triggered the Lodestone has been collapsed? The Corruption of Collapse cannot be evaded, not even by those like us. That poor existence who reached that far will have the very code of their being rewritten before they even realize it. Quick, merciful, and easy."
HUUM!
His words were spoken with a casual, brutal ease.
Valkyrie remained silent for a moment before she asked, "Who do you think it was? A Living Existence? An Early Creature? A Fold Dweller...?"
The burly Commander looked at her, then at the others, a flicker of impatience in his eyes.

"Commander Valkyrie, does it really matter? Come on, let us report this. This is one of the few signals we have received in the last few years. Having the collapse of a Lodestone now means that things are happening soon, after all these eons."
He stood, his massive frame radiating a new energy.
"We have to share this information with the other Early Living Sectors. And as always... we do what we do for the sake of Civilization."
At his words, Valkyrie's expression shifted, her personal sadness giving way to a shared, ancient purpose.
She nodded. "All for the sake of Civilization."
One by one, the others rose, their voices a chorus of profound, unwavering reverence.
"All for the sake of Civilization."
A blinking, collapsed Lodestone.
A single, red light in a sea of green. It was a sign of change, a harbinger of the end of their long, silent vigil.
The thing they had been preparing for, the thing they had sacrificed much to escape, was finally, after all these eons, arriving.
The Fallout!
Organizations for the greater good...humanity's most successful group delusion.
"We're doing this for everyone," they say, while usually doing it for about twelve people in a seat of power.
It's the equivalent of "this will hurt me more than it hurts you" while the person that was saying this...was holding a very large stick.
But what if someone actually meant it? What if the greater good was genuine belief? The conviction required would be either inspiring or terrifying, possibly both!
In the Earliest Folds, there was a time when THE Creature sat in a domain that defied conventional description.
Millions of Inevitabilities swirled around it like a whirlpool of hunger made manifest!
THE Creature smiled at them...not the condescending smile of superiority but the genuine warmth of greeting old friends.
Occasionally, it would reach out and touch their writhing tendrils with the casual affection one might show to passing cats.
An unknown Fold Dweller sat across from THE Creature, trying very hard not to think about how many ways they could cease to exist in this place!
They had come with the ultimate question, the one that had driven them across impossible distances to ask the one being that might actually know the answer.
"What is the truth about Existence? How...should one experience existence to the fullest?"

There, nine massive crimson thrones, each carved from a single, solidified concept of command, were arranged in a circle.
From each throne, crimson-gold lines of pure, informational light shot out, connecting to the myriad of massive, elemental trees.
She drifted towards one of the empty thrones, her gaze sweeping over the other eight Early Creatures who were already seated.
Some were lost in deep cultivation, the faint, shimmering light of one or even multiple Principles surrounding them like halos of impossible power.
Each of them, like her, wore a crimson robe, and each of them radiated a power that was well in excess of 2000 Quadrillion!
"Any changes today?" she asked, her voice a quiet question to the empty air.
The same disembodied, monotone voice replied.
"No, Commander.
Just like all the eons before.
No changes."
Valkyrie hummed and nodded, a familiar, almost weary, ritual.
She settled into her throne, and as she did, illusory crimson-gold screens rose before her, displaying a cascade of information.
She scanned the data, her eyes taking in the endless stream of reports.
Everything was green.
Every system was nominal.
Every projection was stable.
"Give me the daily report," she said.
"Daily Report: Everythings harvested in the last cycle: 1.9 Million Units.
All monitored zones continue to be oversaturated with a surplus of Everythings.
Distribution protocols are operating at 30% capacity to avoid systemic overload."
Valkyrie nodded with a faint, satisfied smile.
The system worked.
The great engine they had built was not just stable; it was overwhelmingly successful.
But at this moment, shockingly...
BZZT!
An alarm!
A shrill, discordant sound that had no place in this realm of perfect, unchanging order.
It was a sound none of them had heard in their lifetimes.
Valkyrie and the other eight Commanders were jolted from their serene contemplation, their eyes snapping open, their expressions a mixture of confusion and dawning alarm.
Valkyrie's hands flew across her screens, her fingers a blur as she pulled up the system overview.
It was a vast, holographic chart showing hundreds of glowing green nodes of light.
And there, in a distant, almost forgotten sector, was one node that was not green.
It was cracked, and it was shining with a frantic, angry red.
Her eyes widened in genuine surprise.
"It seems," she murmured, her voice a low, disbelieving whisper, "something managed to get near a Lodestone and even interrupt its functions.
Its Corruption of Collapse has already been triggered..."
The other Commanders were stirring, their calm facades cracking.
"This...has not happened before, has it?" one of them commented, his voice a low rumble.
Another nodded, his form a shimmering mirage of heat and power.
"No.
When such a thing occurs, the protocol is to let those above us know and to initiate the Closure Protocols.
We begin closing the Doorways designated for us to monitor.
We have collections of hundreds of times the Everythings we expected, anyway.
Far exceeding any parameters."
Valkyrie nodded, a strange, melancholic sadness in her eyes.
"I will pass the word on.
It is just... sad."
A burly, muscular Early Creature, seated on a throne to her right laughed with a harsh, grating sound.
"Why is it sad, Valkyrie?
Because the existence who triggered the Lodestone has been collapsed?
The Corruption of Collapse cannot be evaded, not even by those like us.
That poor existence who reached that far will have the very code of their being rewritten before they even realize it.
Quick, merciful, and easy."
HUUM!
His words were spoken with a casual, brutal ease.
Valkyrie remained silent for a moment before she asked, "Who do you think it was?
A Living Existence?
An Early Creature?
A Fold Dweller...?"
The burly Commander looked at her, then at the others, a flicker of impatience in his eyes.
"Commander Valkyrie, does it really matter?
Come on, let us report this.
This is one of the few signals we have received in the last few years.
Having the collapse of a Lodestone now means that things are happening soon, after all these eons."
He stood, his massive frame radiating a new energy.
"We have to share this information with the other Early Living Sectors.
And as always... we do what we do for the sake of Civilization."
At his words, Valkyrie's expression shifted, her personal sadness giving way to a shared, ancient purpose.
She nodded.
"All for the sake of Civilization."
One by one, the others rose, their voices a chorus of profound, unwavering reverence.
"All for the sake of Civilization."
A blinking, collapsed Lodestone.
A single, red light in a sea of green.
It was a sign of change, a harbinger of the end of their long, silent vigil.
The thing they had been preparing for, the thing they had sacrificed much to escape, was finally, after all these eons, arriving.
The Fallout!
Organizations for the greater good...humanity's most successful group delusion.
"We're doing this for everyone," they say, while usually doing it for about twelve people in a seat of power.
It's the equivalent of "this will hurt me more than it hurts you" while the person that was saying this...was holding a very large stick.
But what if someone actually meant it?
What if the greater good was genuine belief?
The conviction required would be either inspiring or terrifying, possibly both!
In the Earliest Folds, there was a time when THE Creature sat in a domain that defied conventional description.
Millions of Inevitabilities swirled around it like a whirlpool of hunger made manifest!
THE Creature smiled at them...not the condescending smile of superiority but the genuine warmth of greeting old friends.
Occasionally, it would reach out and touch their writhing tendrils with the casual affection one might show to passing cats.
An unknown Fold Dweller sat across from THE Creature, trying very hard not to think about how many ways they could cease to exist in this place!
They had come with the ultimate question, the one that had driven them across impossible distances to ask the one being that might actually know the answer.
"What is the truth about Existence?
How...should one experience existence to the fullest?"

chapters.title: Chapter 4244 Noah Osmont! I
paragraphs: The Inevitabilities paused in their swirling, as if even mindless hunger recognized the weight of the question.
THE Creature was silent for a moment that could have been seconds or centuries...time got nervous around questions that fundamental.
"Existence," THE Creature finally replied, its voice carrying the certainty of someone stating physical law, "is best experienced as a Civilization."
HUUM!
The Fold Dweller waited for elaboration. The Inevitabilities resumed their dance.

"Not just best experienced," THE Creature continued, "but one can only attain the true height of existence as a Civilization and nothing else. Individual achievement, personal transcendence, singular power...these are rehearsals for the real performance. Shadows cast by the actual flame."
The statement landed with the weight of revelation that rewrote previous understandings.

"A Civilization is existence recognizing itself through countless perspectives simultaneously. It's the existence developing eyes numerous enough to actually see itself. One being, no matter how powerful, sees existence from one angle. A Civilization sees it from millions, billions, infinite angles, creating a composite image that approaches truth."
THE Creature touched another passing Inevitability, and for a moment, it seemed less like a singular entity and more like a collective pretending to be one.

"The height of existence isn't reached by climbing alone but by building something that lifts everyone. Not because it's moral or good, but because it's the only way to actually get there. The peak requires all perspectives, all contributions, all failures and successes compiled into something greater than summation."

If this was true...if Civilization was the genuine path to existence's heights, then those who devoted themselves entirely to that goal weren't just altruistic. They were playing a different game entirely...right?
Every selfish being thinking only of themselves was essentially existence experiencing a local maximum, a hill it mistook for the mountain.
Meanwhile, those working for Civilization were climbing the actual peak, even if they couldn't see it yet.
The will required for such dedication would be staggering. To subsume personal desire not from weakness but from understanding that personal achievement was literally incomplete achievement.
To build something you might never see completed because the building itself was the point.
How close were such beings to the true experience of Existence?
Perhaps closer than those with quadrillions in complexity who stood alone. Perhaps the weakest member of a true Civilization experienced more of existence than the strongest solitary entity.
But here's where it gets complicated.

If everyone needs to work together to achieve true existence, and THE Creature knew this, and THE Living Existences presumably knew this, then why all the conflict? Why the imprisonments, the collapses, the endless competition?
Perhaps because knowing the destination and wanting to go there are different things.
It's like knowing exercise is good for you while sitting on the couch eating chips...the knowledge doesn't automatically translate to action.
Or perhaps, and this is the truly unsettling possibility...they were building a Civilization.
Just not one that included everyone.
The greater good, after all, never specifies greater for whom.
The unknown Fold Dweller left that meeting with THE Creature carrying a truth that would either inspire unity or justify the most terrible exclusion.
Because if Civilization was the only path to true existence, then the question became: who gets to be part of the Civilization, and who becomes the foundation it's built upon?
The Inevitabilities continued their swirling, hungry and patient, perhaps understanding better than anyone that even Civilizations needed to eat.
Darkness.
This was all that Noah felt.
It was not the oppressive, hungry black of a void, but a soft, welcoming darkness, a gentle, velvety blanket that promised an end to struggle.
With it came a profound, seductive sense of relief!
As if in this perfect, silent nothingness, everything would finally be okay.
That maybe, just maybe, all he needed to do was let go.
If he let go, wouldn't everything be that much easier? No more fighting against the crushing weight of existence. No more desperate scramble for power against a predetermined doom.
No more shouldering the fate of his family, his people, his very reality. Just... release.
So just... let go.
Let go?
Let go?!
HUUM!
Who was he?
He was Noah fucking Osmont.
He did not let go!
BOOM!
In the heart of that seductive darkness, a defiant, endless blue light shone.
The false peace shattered, consumed by a guttural roar that erupted from the very core of his being!
He rose from the depths of that tempting oblivion, his will a raging inferno against the gentle night.
He saw the brightening blue light, a vast, boundless ocean of pure potential, and he reached for it. He grasped it!
Mana. Oh, Mana!
HUUM!
It was his essence, his birthright, the one infinite truth in a universe of limitations.
He held onto this endless blue sea, and in its boundless depths, he found his anchor, his reason.
'Letting go was never my Way,' his thoughts were a silent, tyrannical bellow.
'Dying simply was never my Way. Am I not chasing an infinite path of elevation? An Infinite Way of Existence?! So why the hell would I go peacefully?!'
BOOM!
His very existence roared in defiance. He grasped at that endless blue light, and the world reformed around him.
He found himself floating in an endless blue sea, a realm of pure, liquid mana that stretched to an infinite horizon.
His body was blanketed by this sea, held in a gentle, yet absolute, stasis. He could not move. He could not act. He could only observe.
The sea was a thing of breathtaking, impossible beauty.
At its far edges, where infinity began, great rivers of shimmering gold flowed, feeding into the blue expanse.
And as he looked closer, he saw it. An outline, an etching in the fabric of this mana-sea, a symbol of impossible, rule-breaking power.
The Seed Glyph of the Principle of the Cheating Architect.
The moment he ascertained this, reality itself seemed to pause, and a new voice, the calm, analytical voice of his own internal system, began its report.
|Emergency Protocol Initiated by [The Principle of the Cheating Architect].|
|Analysis: A catastrophic, existence-altering corruption event has been detected. Standard defensive protocols are insufficient.|
|A single moment of your existence, the instant of corruption, is being expanded. Powered by your [Infinite Mana], this instant is being stretched towards a state of effective Infinity.|

chapters.title: Chapter 4245 Noah Osmont! II
paragraphs: |Current Status: You are now in a pocket of timeless contemplation. The external existence is, for all intents and purposes, paused.|
|Threat Assessment: [Corruption of Collapse] from the Primordial Lodestone.|
|Nature of Threat: Absolute. The corruption seeks to rewrite your fundamental Code of Existence to that of pure, irreversible collapse.|

|Projected Outcome: The rewriting of your code is absolute. It will occur regardless if your complexity exceeded 1,000 or 10,000 Quadrillion. This is not a battle of power, but of fundamental programming.|
Noah received this information, this pronouncement of his own inevitable unmaking, and yet he remained calm.
He was a prisoner in his own existence, a spectator to his own execution. He could do nothing!
|Counter-Strategy Initiated by [The Cheating Architect].|

|Logic: Instead of fighting the [Corruption of Collapse], which is a futile endeavor, [The Cheating Architect] seeks to redirect it. To allow the alteration of your Code of Existence, but into something controllable and even potentially beneficial.|
|Feasibility: A feat of impossibility. The Architect is currently seeking the means to make it possible.|
|Action: [The Cheating Architect] is calling upon your connected weavings of Existence that could potentially be beneficial in this occasion.|
|The Weavings of Ruination have been called forth.|
|The Weavings of the Infiniverse have been called forth.|
|Analyzing all possibilities...|
The blue-gold light of the sea stretched out towards infinity, and in the distance, two concerned, illusory figures appeared.
Ruination, her form a symphony of beautiful, tragic endings. The Infiniverse, a being of countless, interconnected possibilities.
They blazed with a brilliant light as they came into contact with his suspended form, their very essence gushing out in waves of blue-gold support.
A humming buzz continued to echo in Noah's senses as Cheats continued its analysis.
Time passed. But what was time here? Was it passing at all in this stretch of infinity? He was suspended, a thought in an endless moment.
He began to think, his mind, now free from the immediate threat, drifting to the very nature of this state, this Time.
The idea that time was not a constant, but a variable, a river that could be bent and shaped by gravity, by velocity.

One's perception of time is relative to their frame of reference. An observer falling into a black hole would experience their entire future in an instant, while from the outside, they would appear to be frozen for eternity.
'Am I... falling into an endless hole of my own existence right now?'
The epiphany was a quiet, profound thing in the endless blue, his mind buzzing with possibilities!
After what felt like hours, and years, and no time at all, a new set of prompts bloomed.
|A potential solution has been reached on dealing with the [Corruption of Collapse].|
|The Subject, Ruination, shall take on the alteration of collapse.|
BOOM!
The blue sea seethed. Noah's existence buzzed. What?!
|The Subject, Ruination, sees this end and collapse as something inherently critical to her nature. She has willingly volunteered as she states Master, an ending is only another beginning.|
|Alongside the Subject, Ruination, 50% of all the computing capabilities of the Infiniverse have been added to the mix for stability.|
|As the [Corruption of Collapse] has already permeated across your existence, other parts of you must be given into the mix to forge a beneficial product from this calamity.|
|Systems of Existence under you are either partially or fully going to be fused and integrated.|
|The alteration of the Code of Existence and the units of Everythings contained in the Lodestone will be utilized and directed into the final product.|

|Lastly, [The Cheating Architect] will stabilize everything. It has sacrificed the workings of the Agent Architect of [Tyrannical Sovereign] under it, adding the potential and complexity of that unformed Principle into the mix.|
|Analyzing...|
HUUM!
Noah felt the blue-gold seas seethe and tremble!
The illusory figures of Ruination and the Infiniverse scattered into a billion points of light, a torrent of pure potential that fused into his very being.
After what felt like the passage of years, a final prompt rose.
|Trillions of possibilities have been analyzed and theorized, all pointing towards the same result. Proceeding.|
Noah felt his existence stand on a grand precipice. And then...
|Rebooting Existence.|
One last prompt. His perception blanked out.
He felt nothing, and then he felt everything.
He was a child again, feeling the sting of his father's hand after he was drunk and hitting anything in sight, the warmth of his mother's embrace as she told him that everything would be okay.
He was a young man, going to school, going to work, a faceless cog in a machine he didn't understand. He was a Hunter, his hands trembling as he delved into his first dungeon.
He saw it all, a river of memories, of records, of lives lived and unlived.
Until, after what felt like forever, he woke up.
The first thing he noticed was his own eyes. His pupils were pulsing, intricate blue-gold lines constantly being etched and re-etched across their surface.
He was in the endless sea of blue, but this time, he could move.
He sat up, the liquid mana parting around him.
As he acclimated, he noticed it. In the bottom right corner of his vision, a blue holographic display.
It showed a swirling, crimson-blue circle, a globe filled with surging authorities.
Above it, his name floated.
Below it, his Complexity and Purity. A compass, a set of cooldown timers, a network of interconnected status bars.
And in the top left corner of his vision... a cluster of pulsing, crimson-blue light that looked like a series of overlapped infinity symbols. It pulsed with a soft, steady rhythm.
He focused on it.
|Welcome back, Master.|
A voice. A prompt. But the voice was different. It was a perfect, chilling fusion of Ruination's dark, melodic elegance and the System's cool, monotone precision.
He blinked, his eyes shining. "Ruination?"
The reply was instantaneous, the voice both familiar and utterly new.

|Yes, and No, Master. I am RUIN, and I am also EDEN. I am RUIN/EDEN, your personalized System of Existence, born of Ruination, the Infiniverse, the Architect of Tyrannical Sovereign, the Code of Existence of a Lodestone, an unknown number of Everythings, and all other Systems of Existence under your being, all stabilized by the weavings of The Cheating Architect.|
HUUM!
