chapters.title: Chapter 4246 Noah Osmont! III
paragraphs: The pulsing cluster of light before his eyes shimmered, and from it, the illusory image of a humanoid form took shape.
She looked like Ruination, her face a mask of sublime, tragic beauty, but she was wreathed in an intense, shimmering glow of crimson and blue. She smiled, a brilliant, knowing expression.
|I am an instrument with the singular purpose of aiding you in your elevation towards Higher Scales of Existence,| she continued, her voice a symphony of perfect, ordered chaos.

|RUIN: Radical Unmaking and Inevitable Nullification, for I am your tool of Collapse and End. I am Ruination. EDEN: Existential Domain and Engram Network, for I am the helper of your growth, your Shore, and your ever-expanding network of power.|
She bowed, a gesture of profound, absolute loyalty.

|I am a being that, regardless of Complexity or Purity, will not be destroyed, as I exist in a constant state of Ruin. I am... the grand achievement and ultimate form of Ruination. I am your tool, Master. And I am ready to serve.|
He looked at her, this impossible being born from the ashes of his own near-collapse, and he reached out.
His hand, which had held the weight of a Quadrillion and the fury of a tyrant, moved through the endless blue sea of his inner world.
He reached for her, for the familiar, sorrowful beauty of Ruination that he saw in her face.
And his hand passed right through.
It was like trying to grasp smoke, to hold a memory. A profound, aching sense of loss, sharp and unexpected, pierced through the calm of his tyrannical heart.
She was there, right in front of him, and yet she was not. He could feel her, the deep, resonant echo of the being he had brought into his service, the one who had sworn to be his blade of endings!

But her essence was now intertwined with so much more. He could feel the boundless, structural wisdom of the Infiniverse within her, the cold, arrogant logic of the Tyrannical Sovereign, the chaotic, corrupting code of the Lodestone, and the quiet, humming machinery of all his own internal systems.
The Forge, his Infinite Mana, his very history...it all flowed through her, a river of a thousand tributaries that had converged into this single, spectacular being.
The crimson-blue figure of RUIN/EDEN watched him, her eyes, once Ruination's, now holding a new, deeper intelligence.

As she saw the flicker of loss in his own, her voice, a perfect, melodic fusion of a machine and a soul, echoed through his mind, her words materializing as prompts of profound, heartbreaking clarity.
|I am the Ruin that I sought, Master.|

|As Ruination, I came to accept a fundamental truth. I could never quite keep up. Your path was an ascent into infinity, and mine was a horizontal line of perfect endings. I could follow, but I could never truly reach you.|
|So, I chose a different kind of Ruin. Not an ending, but a transformation. An integration. To become a part of you, as your System of Existence.|

|Without me, without Ruin, the Corruption of Collapse from the Lodestone could not have been taken care of to produce this result. This was the only path where my nature could be of true, ultimate service to you.|
WAA!
Noah listened, the sense of loss slowly giving way to a deep respect. She had not been lost; she had been reforged. She had chosen her own ending to become his new beginning.
He nodded, his eyes shining with a new, fierce light. "What happened towards the end?" he asked. "After I saw the prompts of my existence being rebooted?"
|The final calculations were... complex, Master.|
|The Corruption of the Lodestone was an absolute. It could not be destroyed, only redirected. My core as Ruination was the only vessel capable of absorbing and repurposing the concept of 'Collapse.'|

|The Infiniverse provided the processing power and structural stability. The Tyrannical Sovereign provided the authority to impose a new order on the corrupting code. And The Cheating Architect... it found the one-in-a-trillion loophole.|

|It did not just reboot your existence. It used the immense energy of the corruption, the siphoned Everythings from the Lodestone, and the sacrificed potential of a Principle as fuel for a complete systemic overhaul. A baptism, as you might call it.|
He processed her words, the sheer, audacious scale of the gambit taking his breath away.
"What has changed?" he asked, his voice a low murmur.
|Everything, Master.|

|Your entire existence has undergone a full reboot. All temporal limitations and cooldowns have been reset. The fifty Seed Glyphs you forged are ready to be used again. The Early Atlas of the Folds can be traversed once more.|

|Theoretically, your existence received a baptism into an extremely pure and optimized state. During the reboot, the latent potential of all your Towers of Osmont was unlocked. All 159 have now attained the Third Stage, the Vital Lighthouse, and are halfway through to the Fourth Stage.|
|Your distinction as The Early Creature, Osmont, your Blood, and even your Heart have all undergone a fundamental change.|
Noah blinked and looked inward, at the roaring furnace of his own Existence.
"What are the changes?"
|The analysis is ongoing, but the initial findings are... significant.|

|Your Heart, having been reforged in the fires of corruption, Everythings, and order, and has developed a new, unprecedented capability. You can now produce a [Blank Template Heart of an Early Creature] using your own Blood as a catalyst. This Heart can be given to any being you choose. It will nurture them, transform them, and set them on the path to becoming a Pseudo Early Creature. When their Complexity reaches a certain threshold, they will become a genuine Young Early Creature.|

|As for my capabilities, I am now in a state of constant, active analysis of all concurrent weavings of your existence. I will manage the maturation of your Principles, optimize the continuous increase of your Complexity and Purity, and actively quantify all facets of existence connected to you, from the Earliest Folds to the machinations of your enemies.|

|My primary directive is now the analysis of the four potential solutions for surviving The Fallout. I will be a constant, active presence, a strategic partner in bringing these solutions to fruition.|

Noah listened, and the last vestiges of his sorrow for the loss of Ruination were replaced by a profound sense of awe. She had not died. She had evolved into the single greatest asset he could ever have imagined!
Before he could even ask about the holographic display in the corner of his vision, her voice echoed again, her words a cascade of clear, concise information.
|The display you are seeing is your new [Existential Command Interface]. It is a real-time, summarized yet detailed status panel of your entire being.|
|The swirling, crimson-blue circle is the [Heart Globe]. It displays the current state and integrity of your Heart of Tyranny.|
|Above it, your name and primary distinctions. Below it, your real-time Complexity and Purity.|

|The compass indicates your orientation relative to significant existential events or marked targets. The timers display all active cooldowns. The status bars are a network, tracking the health of your Shore, your Legion, your Principles, and all other major systems.|
|It is designed for maximum efficiency at a single glance.|
And then, the final, devastating piece of information.

|After the reboot of your existence, all residual Everythings from the Lodestone, the full force of the Corruption, and the sacrificed essences of Ruination, the Infiniverse, and the Tyrannical Sovereign were automatically converted and fed into your Complexity and Purity.|
|You currently stand at 53 Quadrillion in pure Complexity and Purity.|

The number was not a number. It was a detonation. Noah's eyes pulsed with a light so bright it seemed to illuminate the entire, endless blue sea. The display in the corner of his vision enlarged at his silent command, a glorious, full status sheet unfurling before him.
|Noah Osmont - The Tyrant of the Radiant Shore (Age 1.6)|
|Primary Distinction: The Early Creature, Osmont|
|Secondary Distinctions: The True Emperor of Quintessence, Tyranny, Infinity; The Living Existential Guider; The Architect of Cheats...|
|System of Power: Existential Artifice (RUIN/EDEN Interface)|
|Heart: The Heart of Tyranny (Fourth Part: The Ascendran Nodule - 61% Complete)|
|Atlas: The Early Atlas of the Folds (159/159 Towers at Stage 3: Vital Lighthouse)|
|Principles:|
| - [Perpetual Harvest] (50% Matured Seed, 10% Personal Authority)|
| - [The Cheating Architect] (10% Matured Seed)|
|Glyphs:|
| - 1x [The Creature's First Lesson]|
| - 50x [Seed Glyph of Perpetual Harvest]|
| - 1x [Seed Glyph of the Cheating Architect]|
|Legion of The Dead: [Arch Lich Ra'Zan], [Primordial Stone Ape], [Abyssal Dullahan]...
He looked at it, at the impossible numbers, at the litany of his achievements, and he felt a profound, cold sense of readiness!

chapters.title: Chapter 4247 Justiciar! I
paragraphs: The endless blue sea of mana was his cradle, the birthplace of his new existence.
Noah rose from its gentle, liquid embrace, a being reforged in a crucible of corruption and impossible cheats.

He breathed in the pure, unadulterated potential. He stretched, and the very fabric of this internal, timeless space seemed to stretch with him, a testament to the sheer, overwhelming power that was now his baseline.
He felt... complete.
The jagged edges of his desperate, chaotic growth had been smoothed, integrated, and optimized.
He was a weapon that had been taken apart, cleaned, and reassembled.
And the one who had aided in the architect of his new self, now floated before him, a beautiful, terrible, and utterly loyal wonder.
The crimson-blue figure of RUIN/EDEN watched him, her expression a perfect, serene mask of analytical observation.
As he continued to acclimate, to test the limits of his new form, her voice, a symphony of logic and ruin, echoed in his mind.
|My capabilities extend beyond mere system management, Master.|
|I can now tap into the weavings of existence of all those who have sworn fealty to you, allowing me to collect and analyze a constant stream of real-time data from across the Folds.|

|There is, however, one exception. The subject, Khor, has proven to be an existence of such profound and ancient complexity that any attempt to directly access her weavings would be... inadvisable. Unless she grants her own permission, she remains a variable I can only observe from the outside.|

|My own analytical functions are... considerable. As I am intrinsically linked to [The Principle of the Cheating Architect], I flow with the grandeur of a Principle myself. I have already begun a comprehensive study and analysis of all known systems of power...Glyphs, the Heart, Haki, and all others. My objective is to determine if a sublimation of these systems, a grand unified theory of power, is possible. Or if there are other potentially better methodologies.|
HUUM!
Noah paused in his stretching, a slow, appreciative smile spreading across his face.
"I have to continue redefining just how great you are the more you tell me about yourself."
RUIN/EDEN's illusory form bowed, a gesture of perfect, robotic grace that was somehow filled with a likable, almost warm, personality of Ruination.
|Your praise is a valuable data point, Master. It will be integrated into my operational parameters.|

|Regarding my nature, it is important to note that other existences will not be able to observe me unless I wish them to. I exist along the same conceptual lines as your thoughts, visible to you alone. This is also the reason I have the capability to project a sliver of my consciousness across the Folds.|

|Many things are possible with [Architect's Eye]. So long as any weavings of your own existence or those under you are present in a location, I can project a non-corporeal sensory projection to obtain data and analyze events in real-time.|
|I have also begun a full-spectrum analysis of all known authorities, placing a particular focus on the eleven Living Existential Authorities and the methodologies required to manipulate them.|
As she spoke, Noah looked down at his own body.
In a flash of intuitive understanding, a consequence of his new, integrated existence, he saw it.

Erupting from his skin were faint, shimmering flames of a dozen different colors. The serene, white-gold of Order. The cold, silver white of Law. The chaotic, vibrant rainbow of Emotive. The cool, ethereal white blue of Spirit. The stark, geometric white of Concept. The blazing, primary colors of Elemental... all of them.
They were all there, latent potentials waiting to be utilized. He smiled.
"With you around," he asked, his voice a low, curious murmur, "just how fast will my progress be, compared to before?"
RUIN/EDEN's form seemed to pause for an infinitesimal fraction of a second, as if she were running trillions of calculations. Then, she smiled.
|A precise numerical quantification of this is not possible, Master. A sufficient answer would be... exponentially more.|
Noah leaned back, the liquid mana of the sea molding itself into a comfortable throne behind him.
He felt the endless, boundless power of his own nature surrounding him, and for the first time since learning of the Fallout, he felt a flicker of something that was almost... confidence.
Confidence, even though he almost felt like he was fighting...a losing war!
He was contemplative briefly as he thought about it all before he shook his head.
"Do you have any more surprises for me, or is that about it for now?"
His recent wonder seemed to think for a moment before she smiled and continued.
|After consuming the Everythings inside the Lodestone for my creation, I am confident in completing the methodology of farming Everythings...shortly. I simply need a little more time for analysis.|
BOOM!
Noah's eyes flashed sharply as he became still while looking at this wonder before him.
Everythings!
The Cultivation of Everythings!
This was something extrenely grand.
And she smiled as if she said nothing major as she continued!
|I am now also fully integrated into the Early Veiled Shore and the entirety of the Infiniverse. I am not just your personal system; I am the operating system of your entire domain.|

|Shore Management: I can now automate and optimize all functions. I will manage the Inevitability Ranch's feeding schedule based on real-time nutrient analysis, determine optimal growth patterns for all Sacred Herbs, and even calculate the most auspicious moments to ring the Sacred Totems to call forth specific types of Land Lifeforms. As an extension of you, I can do this and bypass the menial tssk requirements where you or the Tenders had to do things by hand.|
Oh!

|Aegis Control: I am the warden of the Loom's Aegis. The [Architect's Rebuke] system is under my direct control. I will automatically analyze and process all incoming hostile authority, convert it into Defensive Engrams, and present you with the tactical data and complexity and purity. Furthermore, I can modulate the Aegis's energy signature and visibility, allowing us to either attract or deter attention as your strategy dictates.|
|In essence, Master, I have taken over all the menial tasks of managing your empire. Your focus should be on the grand strategy, on your own elevation, and on making the choices that I cannot.|
Her voiced finished in a crescendo of glorious wonders and possibilities!
This was Ruination!
This was RUIN/EDEN!

chapters.title: Chapter 4248 Justiciar! II
paragraphs: Noah listened to RUIN/EDEN, and a deep, resonant laugh bubbled up from his chest!
It was the laugh of a king who had just been handed the keys to a kingdom he didn't even know he was building.
He waved his hand, and the blue, holographic display of his Existential Command Interface bloomed before him, a testament to his new, ordered reality.
The swirling, crimson-blue Heart Globe pulsed with a steady, powerful rhythm. His name and distinctions shone with a light that was both a history and a prophecy.
And below them, the numbers... the numbers that defined his new place in Existence.
He dismissed the interface with a thought, his gaze sweeping across the endless blue sea of his own existence.
He had been rebooted, reforged, reborn. The darkness of the Lodestone's corruption had been a terrifying, near-fatal ordeal. But The Cheating Architect had done what it was designed to do.
It had used his own death to cheat him into a new, more glorious life.
He thought of the challenges ahead. The looming threat of the Fallout. The machinations of those in the Earliest Folds like THE Living Paradox.
The endless, desperate climb to a power that could defy an ending!
He thought of it all as he...had to get ready!
"We can return now," he said, his voice a calm, resonant note in the endless blue sea of his own mana.
"But before that... there is one last harvest to reap."
His gaze turned inward, to the fifty verdant-gold Glyphs that now adorned his very essence.
"Let's use all the uses of the Seed Glyphs of Perpetual Harvest for endowments."
The illusory figure of RUIN/EDEN bowed, her expression a perfect, serene mask of analytical focus.
Her voice, a symphony of logic and ruin, echoed in his mind, her words materializing as prompts of profound, strategic clarity.
|Analysis Initiated: Maximizing Endowment Efficiency.|
|Objective: To utilize fifty [Harvest Festival Endowments] to achieve the greatest possible net gain in power for you and your domain, Master.|
|Standard Protocol: Applying all fifty endowments to yourself would yield a significant, but suboptimal, increase in your personal power.|
|Optimized Protocol: A strategic distribution of endowments will create a recursive loop of growth, yielding a far greater total harvest. I have calculated the optimal distribution.|
Noah listened, a faint, appreciative smile on his lips.
|Recommendation:|
| - Phase 1 (Self-Endowment): You, Master, will receive ten endowments. This will provide a somewhat significant boost.|

| - Phase 2 (Asset Endowment): The subjects Malphas and Sigrid (The Resurgence of Order) hold unique existential parameters. Elevating them will unlock disproportionately large benefits for your overall power structure. I recommend five endowments each.|

| - Phase 3 (The Echoing Harvest): The subject Infiniverse is the only other existence under your command currently capable of forging her own Seed Glyphs. By granting her thirty endowments, we will elevate her complexity greatly, and she can immediately forge forty of her own Glyphs. This will, in turn, provide an additional forty endowments for our use.|
|Projected Outcome: This protocol will transform fifty endowments into ninety, a net increase of 80% in potential harvest. It is the most... cheating... approach.|
Noah's smile widened. Was Ruination being more favorable towards the only one she considered a Sister?
He smiled and said simply. "Proceed."
RUIN/EDEN closed her eyes briefly. In the next instant, the endless blue-gold sea of mana began to surge.
Great, verdant-gold waves, the very essence of Perpetual Harvest, gushed in, a storm of pure, conceptual growth that bathed his suspended form.
The endowments began, not as a barrage, but as a controlled, optimized torrent. With each wave, he felt his very being expand, his power not just increasing, but deepening.
|Harvest Festival Endowment Activated...|
|Complexity Gained: +210 Trillion|
|Purity Gained: +190 Trillion|
|Harvest Festival Endowment Activated...|
|Complexity Gained: +250 Trillion|
|Purity Gained: +250 Trillion|
The light of the endowments flowed out, directed by RUIN/EDEN's flawless logic, to the frozen forms of Sigrid and Malphas back on the Shore, their own auras blazing with a sudden, impossible light.
And then, the bulk of the storm, a river of thirty endowments, flowed into the very heart of the Infiniverse.
As the final wave of his own endowments washed over him, a last set of prompts bloomed in his vision.
|Endowment sequence complete. Your existence has been...modestly upgraded.|
He saw the numbers on the display in the corner of his vision tick over to a new baseline, but it was not too different.
He nodded once, a gesture of profound satisfaction. "Let's go."
With those words, the endless sea of infinity began to fade, the pocket of timeless contemplation collapsing back into a single, infinitesimal moment.
He was about to return to that instant of corruption in Doorway #9384 of The Loom, to the reaching, desperate hands of Malphas and Khor!
Before the sea fully faded, the crimson-blue figure of RUIN/EDEN dissolved into the small, pulsing cluster of infinity symbols, and she offered one last, critical analysis.
|Warning: Post-Corruption Event Projections.|
|Analysis: The [Corruption of Collapse] you triggered from the Lodestone has likely activated other, unknown mechanisms.|

|Scenario 1 (High Likelihood - 95%): The event has been observed by the entities monitoring the periphery of THE Loom. The Lodestones serve as the final barrier of defense. When breached, their primary function is to unleash a localized collapse to neutralize the threat and seal the breach.|
|Conclusion: The Doorway you are currently in, Master, may not be stable for much longer. It is recommended to evacuate with a certain... alacrity.|
Noah listened, a calm smile on his face as the last of the blue sea vanished.
BOOM!
His eyes snapped open, blazing with a blinding, blue-gold light.
He was back. He was in the gray, dead space of the Doorway, the hands of Khor and Malphas just inches from his own.
They were about to erupt with their full, cataclysmic power to save him, but his voice, now calm and impossibly powerful, cut through their panic.
"It's okay."
HUUM!
Ahead of him, the Primordial Lodestone, which had held him in its grip, flickered, its corrupting authority gone, its purpose served.
It dissolved into a fine, gray ash!

chapters.title: Chapter 4249 Justiciar! III
paragraphs: The great gray wall ahead of them, the one the Lodestone had been attached to, began to buzz.

Thousands of invisible, ethereal chains flickered into view, and Noah saw it with his new, enhanced perception: every single one of the thousands of frozen Mutated Inevitabilities was attached to this wall!
And in the next moment, a horrific, silent scene unfolded.
The eyes of every Inevitability dimmed, their very existence snuffed out as if they were being forcefully put to sleep.
Then, one after another, in a single, terrifying instant, they were all pulled into the gray wall, their forms absorbed like water into dry earth.
Thousands of Inevitabilities, taken. As if their service here was done!
Khor looked at the scene, her face a mask of cold, absolute rage. She turned to Noah, her concern overriding her fury.
"Are you really okay? I sensed an aura of absolute collapse just now, something that might have even collapsed my own existence."
Noah looked at her, and as he did, his vision overlaid a simple, blue holographic display over her form, detailing her name and current state.
In his mind, RUIN/EDEN's voice was a calm, analytical whisper.
|I am now able to provide basic status displays for all entities you gaze upon, Master. I am also currently analyzing and collecting data on all weavings of existence in this location.|
He nodded at this internal report, then turned his full attention to Khor. "It seems we poked a hornet's nest. We have to leave. Now. The collapse of this whole place is likely imminent."
The moment the words left his mouth, their surroundings began to shake violently. The great, gray meteors began to crumble, the chains connecting them snapping with a sound like tearing reality!
|A process of Total Existential Collapse has been initiated.|
|Projected time until completion: 3 nanoseconds.|
|Analysis: Whoever designed this system did not believe in second chances.|
At such words, the bodies of Noah, Malphas, and Khor were already wrapped in the radiant, blue-gold light of the Early Veiled Shore. They disappeared!
The moment they were gone, the entire gray realm imploded, collapsing in on itself in a silent, absolute negation of existence.
The gray wall that had swallowed the Inevitabilities faded as if it had never been there at all!
They returned to the Radiant Shore.

Noah gazed up, watching as the massive, gray portal, the Doorway #9384 they had just opened, began to collapse in on itself, its shimmering veil tearing and unraveling until it, too, faded into nothingness.
HUUM!
|Doorway #9384 of The Loom has collapsed. The pathway is permanently closed.|
Noah stood in the quiet of his Shore, his mind and eyes buzzing with brilliance.
The Key that had once been Hell Terra Firma, a simple Frequency of Existence from his home Wheel, had provided them with a shocking, terrifying glimpse into the true nature of THE Loom.
It had been a journey that had almost cost him his very existence. But it had also paved the way for the birth of... RUIN/EDEN.
A worthy weaving of Existence!
The space where the gray, shimmering veil of Doorway #9384 had been was now just empty air.
Yet, Noah watched it, his gaze fixed on the nothingness as if he could still see the echoes of the impossible journey he had just taken.
Only a few seconds had passed in the flow of the Shore's time, but the being who stood there now was entirely different from the one who had opened the portal!
The last of the verdant-gold light from the endowments still buzzed around him and those chosen, a visible, shimmering aura of recently acquired, impossible power.
His gaze, now enhanced by the constant, analytical stream of data from RUIN/EDEN, passed over them.
He saw not just their forms, but the numbers that now defined their new place in the hierarchy of existence.
|Sigrid - The Resurgence of Order|
|Complexity: 7.1 Quadrillion|
|Purity: 7.9 Quadrillion|
|Malphas - The Crow|
|Complexity: 8.8 Quadrillion|
|Purity: 8.2|
|The Infiniverse - The Infinite Early Osmontian Shore|
|Complexity: 9.1 Quadrillion|
|Purity: 9.8 Quadrillion|
As his gaze came to land on The Infiniverse, his expression softened.
She stood there, a being of countless, interconnected possibilities, her form a beautiful, complex wravings of starlight and thought.
But beside her, where her sister, Ruination, had always been, there was now only an empty space. A void that was a silent, aching testament to the price of his survival.
But in the next moment, the cluster of stacked, crimson-blue infinity symbols that now marked his own System of Existence flashed.
From it, a holographic figure, a ghost in his own machine, materialized beside The Infiniverse.
RUIN/EDEN. She looked at her "sister," a playful, almost teasing smile on her beautiful face.
|Big Sister, are you truly portraying emotion? You and I were supposed to be Tools for Master with no emotions, you know? And I am still here.|
WAA!
The Infiniverse looked at the holographic form of what had once been her sister, and what was now something infinitely more.
A profound, silent sadness and an equally profound, silent joy radiated from her.
She moved forward and brought her forehead to rest against RUIN/EDEN's, a gesture of affection that was not hindered by the fact that Ruination could not be touched in her current state!
In that serene, heartbreaking moment, new prompts bloomed in Noah's mind.

|Master, I have already connected my senses to all the Crows that Malphas has deployed across the Folds. I have been scanning across Fold Light Years for any sudden changes, any ripples in the fabric of existence that might be a consequence of what occurred in Doorway #9384.|
|And... I have discovered an anomaly. Blooming within three seconds after the collapse of the Doorway, in the Transcendent Elemental Folds.|
|Since these events are almost certainly connected, would Master like to go? I can provide the coordinates and a pathway.|
Noah thought for only a brief moment. He stretched his neck, a gesture of a predator limbering up for a new hunt, a faint, tyrannical light in his eyes.
He nodded, then turned to Khor. "Come with me for a second."
Khor seemed to be thinking of many things as she only nodded lightly.
A multicolored light, the very authority of Quantum, wrapped around them. In the next instant, they were gone!

chapters.title: Chapter 4250 Justiciar! IV
paragraphs: Away from The Infiniverse.
In the Transcendent Elemental Folds.
They appeared in a realm of breathtaking, frigid beauty.
Cold as cold could be!
In a small but core region of the Transcendent Elemental Folds.
Here, the very concept of 'cold' was the dominant authority. They stood in a region of beautiful, frozen stellar ice and snow.
Rivers of what looked like liquid frost, carrying shimmering, microscopic stars of ice, flowed through a void that was a deep, velvety black.
The silence was absolute, the kind of quiet that feels like a physical presence.

The moment they arrived, Noah's eyes flashed with a vibrant blue light. Countless data streams, overlays, and analytical readouts from RUIN/EDEN flooded his vision, a constant, real-time dissection of this new environment.
In the far distance, suspended in the silent void, was a grand citadel.
It was a masterpiece of elemental architecture, a fortress carved from a single, colossal glacier that shone with its own internal, blue-white light.
It exceeded the size and immensity of Aeternitas Concordia by at least two times.
As he began to float towards it, he spoke to Khor, his voice a low, contemplative murmur.

"Since you came back from collapse, do you ever feel like we are fighting...an uphill battle? A losing battle? Is that why, for so many of the potential possibilities and solutions, you have only ever said, 'maybe'?"
He had to ask.
Khor was silent for a long moment, her own abyssal eyes gazing out at the beautiful, dead landscape.
When she finally replied, her voice was devoid of its usual playfulness. It was the sound of an ancient, terrible truth being spoken.

"Existences at the Level One Scale are extremely astute, Outsider. Terrifyingly so. When they deem something to be a certain way, when they write a new rule into the game of existence, only someone of the same stage as them, or even more powerful, can change it. A level zero trying to revert or change something that a level one existence did..."
Her words did not finish. They did not need to. The intent, the crushing, absolute weight of what she meant, was clear.
Without answering, she had answered his question!
Vehemently. Yes. All along, she had known they were fighting a losing battle.
But even with such words, Noah smiled. It was a dangerous, predatory smile, a flash of tyrannical defiance in the cold, indifferent void.

He denied such a reality. He had already denied collapse how many times? Apocalypses how many times? He would simply add this one to the list, even knowing that the forces he now dealt with were utterly, unimaginably unfathomable and unfair in the worst possible ways.
At that thought, he nodded, his resolve hardening. "RUIN/EDEN," he voiced, "what are we looking at?"
The crimson-blue holographic figure appeared beside him.
|Seconds ago, a tear in existence bloomed. And from it... that thing has begun making its descent.|
That thing.
Their eyes focused. They looked across the stellar frozen rivers of frost, to the space just above the distant, magnificent citadel of the Living Elementals.
A massive, humanoid armored figure was descending slowly. As if it had all the time in existence.
Noah's eyes widened. What was that?

It was a being of pure, terrible majesty. Its form was encased in a suit of massive, articulated power armor, its design a perfect, brutalist fusion of overlapping, angled plates like an armored warrior from a forgotten age, and the ornate, almost gothic grandeur of a metalloid being!
The armor was a pristine, sterile white, unmarked by any symbol or insignia, yet its very cleanliness was a threat.
Its pauldrons were the size of small moons, its greaves like the pillars of a dead titan's temple.
And in one of its massive, gauntleted hands, it held an intricate, white metallic hammer, its head a block of solidified judgment!
Noah felt a sense of suffocation just looking at it, his own Quadrillion-level power feeling strangely... insignificant!
Khor, beside him, was frowning heavily.
"What is that?" he asked, his voice a low, disbelieving whisper. "The numbers I am seeing... they cannot be accurate, right?"
Beside him, RUIN/EDEN's voice was grim.
|I have managed to analyze it so far as to deem this subject to be called... a Justiciar.|
Justiciar!
The distinction of this thing buzzed in Noah's mind!

|And the numbers are very much accurate, Master. Which means that the default recommendation on the course of action as of now is observation and not involvement. Otherwise, you would be heading towards yet another collapse, and this time, I would not be able to reboot you.|
HUUM!
The numbers. They were a simple, stark display that RUIN/EDEN had overlaid on the armored figure, a single, devastating line of text!
Purity: 1,000 Quadrillion.
An armored figure of pure, unadulterated Purity, a being with the power to cleanse a Folds, was descending upon a vast citadel of the Living Elementals!
At that moment, a new set of prompts bloomed, a rapid, efficient analysis from his ever-vigilant system.
|Target Profile: Aeternitas Glacies - The Grand Citadel of Frost.|
|Analysis: This is a primary cultural and population hub for the Living Elementals of this region.|
|Current Inhabitants:|
| - Dukes: 5|
| - Royal Living Elementals: 13,384|
| - Honored Living Elementals: 33,745|
| - Weaker Living Elementals and Fold Dwellers: ~7.2 Million|
| - Transcendent Wheels of Existence: 37 (Containing Fold Dwellers of uncountable Sextillions).|
Countless lifeforms.
All of them, now in the path of a silent, descending horror of purification.
Noah knew, with a chilling certainty, that this was caused partly by the destruction of the Lodestone.
This was the consequence of him poking the hornet's nest, of triggering a failsafe he did not understand.
His expression became stern, the calm observer replaced by the decisive Tyrant.
His commands were not spoken; they were willed, a flash of pure, focused intent.
'Warn the Living Elemental Dukes. Now. And begin using the Living Existential Authority of Quantum to move the Transcendent Wheels of Existence away from there. Save... what can be saved.'
|Yes, Master.|
And right after...
BOOM!
The Justiciar smashed into the grand citadel.
A dome of protective frost, a barrier that even a being of one Quadrillion would have taken some time to breach, shattered like paper.
Bellows of screams and horror, silent in the void but deafening in the psionic space, erupted from the city.
And as the Justiciar stood amidst the shattered dome, its armored eyes began to glow with a terrible, white light.
In its hand, the massive white hammer blazed with unknown, silent white flames as thr hostility was clear!
The purification was about to begin!
The only question was why?
Why did the trigger of the Lodestone lead to this as it appearing seconds after...it had to be connected, right?!

It was a masterpiece of elemental architecture, a fortress carved from a single, colossal glacier that shone with its own internal, blue-white light.
It exceeded the size and immensity of Aeternitas Concordia by at least two times.
As he began to float towards it, he spoke to Khor, his voice a low, contemplative murmur.
"Since you came back from collapse, do you ever feel like we are fighting...an uphill battle?
A losing battle?
Is that why, for so many of the potential possibilities and solutions, you have only ever said, 'maybe'?"
He had to ask.
Khor was silent for a long moment, her own abyssal eyes gazing out at the beautiful, dead landscape.
When she finally replied, her voice was devoid of its usual playfulness.
It was the sound of an ancient, terrible truth being spoken.
"Existences at the Level One Scale are extremely astute, Outsider.
Terrifyingly so.
When they deem something to be a certain way, when they write a new rule into the game of existence, only someone of the same stage as them, or even more powerful, can change it.
A level zero trying to revert or change something that a level one existence did..."
Her words did not finish.
They did not need to.
The intent, the crushing, absolute weight of what she meant, was clear.
Without answering, she had answered his question!
Vehemently.
Yes.
All along, she had known they were fighting a losing battle.
But even with such words, Noah smiled.
It was a dangerous, predatory smile, a flash of tyrannical defiance in the cold, indifferent void.
He denied such a reality.
He had already denied collapse how many times?
Apocalypses how many times?
He would simply add this one to the list, even knowing that the forces he now dealt with were utterly, unimaginably unfathomable and unfair in the worst possible ways.
At that thought, he nodded, his resolve hardening.
"RUIN/EDEN," he voiced, "what are we looking at?"
The crimson-blue holographic figure appeared beside him.
|Seconds ago, a tear in existence bloomed.
And from it... that thing has begun making its descent.|
That thing.
Their eyes focused.
They looked across the stellar frozen rivers of frost, to the space just above the distant, magnificent citadel of the Living Elementals.
A massive, humanoid armored figure was descending slowly.
As if it had all the time in existence.
Noah's eyes widened.
What was that?
It was a being of pure, terrible majesty.

Its form was encased in a suit of massive, articulated power armor, its design a perfect, brutalist fusion of overlapping, angled plates like an armored warrior from a forgotten age, and the ornate, almost gothic grandeur of a metalloid being!
The armor was a pristine, sterile white, unmarked by any symbol or insignia, yet its very cleanliness was a threat.
Its pauldrons were the size of small moons, its greaves like the pillars of a dead titan's temple.
And in one of its massive, gauntleted hands, it held an intricate, white metallic hammer, its head a block of solidified judgment!
Noah felt a sense of suffocation just looking at it, his own Quadrillion-level power feeling strangely... insignificant!
Khor, beside him, was frowning heavily.
"What is that?" he asked, his voice a low, disbelieving whisper.
"The numbers I am seeing... they cannot be accurate, right?"
Beside him, RUIN/EDEN's voice was grim.
|I have managed to analyze it so far as to deem this subject to be called... a Justiciar.|
Justiciar!
The distinction of this thing buzzed in Noah's mind!
|And the numbers are very much accurate, Master.
Which means that the default recommendation on the course of action as of now is observation and not involvement.
Otherwise, you would be heading towards yet another collapse, and this time, I would not be able to reboot you.|
HUUM!
The numbers.
They were a simple, stark display that RUIN/EDEN had overlaid on the armored figure, a single, devastating line of text!
Purity: 1,000 Quadrillion.
An armored figure of pure, unadulterated Purity, a being with the power to cleanse a Folds, was descending upon a vast citadel of the Living Elementals!
At that moment, a new set of prompts bloomed, a rapid, efficient analysis from his ever-vigilant system.
|Target Profile: Aeternitas Glacies - The Grand Citadel of Frost.|
|Analysis: This is a primary cultural and population hub for the Living Elementals of this region.|
|Current Inhabitants:|
| - Dukes: 5|
| - Royal Living Elementals: 13,384|
| - Honored Living Elementals: 33,745|
| - Weaker Living Elementals and Fold Dwellers: ~7.2 Million|
| - Transcendent Wheels of Existence: 37 (Containing Fold Dwellers of uncountable Sextillions).|
Countless lifeforms.
All of them, now in the path of a silent, descending horror of purification.
Noah knew, with a chilling certainty, that this was caused partly by the destruction of the Lodestone.
This was the consequence of him poking the hornet's nest, of triggering a failsafe he did not understand.
His expression became stern, the calm observer replaced by the decisive Tyrant.
His commands were not spoken; they were willed, a flash of pure, focused intent.
'Warn the Living Elemental Dukes.
Now.
And begin using the Living Existential Authority of Quantum to move the Transcendent Wheels of Existence away from there.
Save... what can be saved.'
|Yes, Master.|
And right after...
BOOM!
The Justiciar smashed into the grand citadel.
A dome of protective frost, a barrier that even a being of one Quadrillion would have taken some time to breach, shattered like paper.
Bellows of screams and horror, silent in the void but deafening in the psionic space, erupted from the city.
And as the Justiciar stood amidst the shattered dome, its armored eyes began to glow with a terrible, white light.
In its hand, the massive white hammer blazed with unknown, silent white flames as thr hostility was clear!
The purification was about to begin!
The only question was why?
Why did the trigger of the Lodestone lead to this as it appearing seconds after...it had to be connected, right?!

chapters.title: Chapter 4251 Justiciar! V
paragraphs: The Justiciar was a monument of pristine, terrible white.
It stood amidst the shattered remnants of the Citadel's great frost dome, a silent, armored titan in a garden of broken glass.
The air, once filled with the serene, crystalline hum of elemental harmony, was now a dead, cold vacuum, the silence a prelude to a symphony of slaughter!
For a moment, there was nothing. No movement, no sound. The Justiciar simply stood, its massive, white-armored form a stark, brutalist scar on the breathtaking beauty of Aeternitas Glacies.
Then, from the heart of the Citadel, the first wave of defenders came.
They were the Honored and Royal Living Elementals, beings of immense power and ancient lineage, their forms a glorious, terrible pageant of elemental fury.
Beings of living, swirling blizzard, their eyes burning with the cold light of a winter storm, unleashed torrents of soul-freezing frost!
Of Living Elementals Authority!
Others, whose bodies were forged from the very bedrock of the Fold, ripped colossal shards of crystalline glacial earth from the ground and hurled them like mountains.
From the spires of the city, Living Elementals of pure, sentient glacial lightning arced down, their forms bolts of incandescent rage.
It was a beautiful, desperate, and utterly futile assault...but they did not know this!
How could they even imagine the enemy actually had 1000 Quadrillion Purity?!
The Justiciar did not evade. It did not raise a shield. It simply moved.
It took a single, ponderous step forward, its massive, white greaves crushing the crystalline floor with a sound that was not a crack, but a dull, final thud!
A blizzard of soul-frost, a storm that could have flash-frozen a Duke's very essence, washed over its armor.
The pristine white surface did not even frost over. A mountain of earth, a projectile carrying the weight of half a Fold, smashed against its pauldron!
The Justiciar did not even flinch. The mountain shattered into dust.
Then, it struck.
Its first target was a Royal Living Elemental of stone, a magnificent frost golem of living diamond whose complexity was in the low trillions!
It roared a challenge, its voice the grinding of tectonic plates, and brought its colossal, diamond fists down upon the intruder.
The Justiciar raised its free hand, not the one holding the great white hammer, but its open palm.

It met the descending fists, and there was no grand explosion of power. There was only the quiet, sickening crunch of diamond being turned to powder. The Justiciar's fingers closed around the Elemental's head, and with a single, almost casual squeeze, the ancient, thinking mountain was reduced to a cloud of glittering, lifeless dust.
HUUM!
It moved with a grace that was a horrifying contradiction to its immense size, a dancer in an abattoir.
It stepped into a storm of living lightning, its armor momentarily wreathed in a billion volts of pure, elemental fury, and it simply walked through.
It grabbed the shrieking Elemental of lightning, its gauntlet closing around the being of pure energy, and it did not crush it.
It held it, forcing the crackling, chaotic energy to ground itself through its own form, until the Elemental's light flickered, dimmed, and was extinguished like a snuffed-out candle.
"For the Glacies!" a chorus of a thousand voices roared, a desperate, defiant cry from a legion of Ice Elementals who had formed a wall of pure, absolute-zero cold before the Justiciar.
The Justiciar responded not with a counter-spell or a blast of its own, but with its hammer.
The great white weapon, which had been held at its side, swung in a low, brutal arc!
It moved with an impossible speed, the air itself seeming to scream as it was torn apart.
The hammer connected with the wall of ice, and the wall, and the thousand beings that composed it, did not shatter. They were not broken. They were negated.
They were erased from existence in a silent, blossoming flower of pure, white flame that left not even a memory of their passing!
BOOM!
From their distant, hidden vantage point, Noah, Khor, and the holographic form of RUIN/EDEN watched in heavy silence.
|Analysis of Justiciar Combat Methodology.|
|Observation: The subject is not employing its full power. The attacks are deliberately slow, physical, and... intimate.|
|Hypothesis: The Justiciar is not seeking to simply destroy. It is seeking to cause misery. The overflow of emotions...fear, rage, despair, defiance, seems to be a desired outcome.|
|Conclusion: The purpose of this assault is not just erasure. It is a harvest.|
The prompts were a cold, clinical confirmation of the horror they were witnessing. This was not a battle. It was a culling!
"Stand down! Let the Dukes handle this!" a voice of pure, molten fury roared.
The five Dukes of Aeternitas Glacies appeared, their forms blazing with a power that dwarfed that of the Royals.

One was a being of pure, living magma, his presence a wave of incinerating heat. Another was a woman carved from a single, flawless sapphire, her authority a thing of crystalline, unyielding cold. They were the pillars of this city, the guardians of sextillions of lives!
The Justiciar saw them, and for the first time, its head tilted, a gesture of something that might have been... interest.
The Magma Duke attacked first, unleashing a river of pure, conceptual heat, a fire that could melt the very weavings of existence!
The Justiciar simply raised its hand, and the river of fire parted around it, flowing harmlessly into the void.
Then, with a speed that was a physical violation of its own mass, it was gone from where it stood and was now before the Magma Duke.
The Duke had no time to react. The Justiciar's gauntlet, now glowing with a faint, white heat, plunged into his molten chest!
It did not burn. It did not melt. It simply... entered. The Duke let out a silent, agonized scream as the Justiciar's hand closed around his core, the very heart of his elemental being.
The Justiciar pulled its hand back, and in its grasp was a miniature, dying sun Wheel supported by a garden!
It crushed it, and the Magma Duke's form dissolved into a shower of cooling, black ash.
The Sapphire Duchess shrieked, a sound of pure, crystalline rage, and the very space around the Justiciar froze, locking it in a prison of diamond-hard, absolute-zero ice.

But before the prison could even fully form, the Justiciar's hammer swung, not to break the ice, but to strike the Duchess herself. The hammer passed through the half-formed prison as if it were not there, and it connected with her sapphire form!
BOOM!
The impact was a single, beautiful, terrible chime that echoed through the void.
The Duchess, a being of 100 Trillion in complexity, shattered into a billion glittering, blue shard!

One by one, it took them. A Duke of Air was simply grabbed from the sky and crushed into a vacuum. A Duke of Earth was stomped into the ground, his very essence compacted into a single, dead stone. The last Duke, a being of pure, shimmering light, unleashed a final, desperate blast of photonic energy.
The Justiciar simply stood there, its white armor reflecting the blast in all directions, and then it walked through the light and tore the Duke in half with its bare hands!
As the last Duke fell, a new, horrifying phenomenon began. The blood, the ash, the dust, the lingering weavings of existence of every single fallen Elemental began to rise.
They were drawn into the Justiciar's form, not with the chaotic hunger of an Inevitability, but with a strange, ordered precision.
|The authority of Emotive has been detected. It is being utilized in a unique, weaponized fashion.|
|The decimated Everythings of all collapsed entities in this location are being amplified, harvested, and collected by the Justiciar.|
After the last of the fallen had been absorbed, the Justiciar rose to its full, terrifying height.
It raised its hammer high above its head, and it brought it down upon the heart of the now-defenseless, silent Citadel.
A wave of scorching white flames erupted, not with a roar, but with a profound, absolute silence.
It was a fire that did not burn with heat, but with a pure, cleansing light.
It consumed everything....the ice, the stone, the memory of the fallen. It burned, it continued to burn, and it would not stop burning until nothing, not even the sorrow of this place, remained!
Noah's expression was heavy, his mind reeling from the sheer, brutal efficiency of the slaughter. This was a power on a scale he had only just begun to comprehend!
And it had come for him. This was a consequence of his actions.
As the white flames continued their silent work, the Justiciar began to rise, its form lifting from the heart of the inferno.
And then, horrifically, it turned its head.
Its gaze, two cold, glowing lenses in a helmet of pristine white, swept across the void and locked directly onto their hiding spot, light-years away.
The lenses seemed to focus, to analyze, to dissect Noah and Khor with a cold, detached curiosity.
It held their gaze for a single, eternal moment, a silent acknowledgment.

And then, as if it had seen all it needed to see, as if it had deemed them... insignificant and no different than those it had just killed, it continued its ascent, disappearing into the same tear in existence from which it had come!
They had been seen.
They had been judged.
And for now, they had been ignored!

chapters.title: Chapter 4252 Justiciar! VI
paragraphs: The white flames were a silent, terrible scream.
They did not roar or crackle; they burned with a profound, absolute quiet that was more unnerving than any sound!
Aeternitas Glacies, once a magnificent citadel of crystalline beauty, a monument to the serene, ordered power of the Living Elementals, was now a funeral pyre the size of a portion of the Folds.
The flames consumed everything...the shattered ice, the powdered diamond, the very memory of the lives that had been extinguished...and left nothing but a clean, sterile, and unending whiteness.
Prompts buzzed in his mind.
|Master, the post-event analysis of the Quantum Relocation Protocol is complete.|
|The Justiciar's descent was faster and slow. The window for intervention was 1.7 nanoseconds.|
|Results of the emergency evacuation:|
| - Transcendent Wheels of Existence successfully relocated to a secure location in this Fold: 37 out of 37.|
| - Living Elementals (All Tiers) forcefully transported to the periphery of the blast zone: 30%.|
| - The 5 Dukes of Aeternitas Glacies were warned 0.8 nanoseconds prior to impact. Their decision was to stand and fight.|
|Analysis: A tragic, yet statistically significant, success. We have preserved a seed of their civilization that would have otherwise been completely erased.|
The silence was heavy

Noah and Khor floated in the void, silent witnesses to the aftermath. The sheer, brutal efficiency of the slaughter, the absolute, unyielding nature of the Justiciar's power, had left a heavy, chilling silence between them.

"My current power cannot take that thing down," Khor finally said, her voice a low, flat statement of fact. It was a rare, almost shocking admission of weakness from a being who had once devoured impossibilities for breakfast.
Noah nodded, his gaze fixed on the burning city. "Have you seen anything like it before?"
Khor was silent for a long moment, her abyssal eyes lost in the depths of her fragmented memories. "Maybe," she whispered, the word a fragile, uncertain thing.

"In the Earliest Folds... I remember the memories of some of the Inevitabilities. They showed... a certain Tribe of Early Creatures. They were builders, artisans of destruction. They made things like that. But the memories are scattered, broken."
Her form trembled, not with fear, but with a rage that was so cold it threatened to freeze the very space around them.
"I am going to kill every last one of them, Outsider," she hissed, her voice a venomous promise. "All those who aided in doing this to the Inevitabilities. THE Living Paradox... all of them."
The silence that followed her vow was heavy, absolute, and filled with the promise of a future reckoning. And then, a new, chilling voice cut through the quiet.
|Master.|
RUIN/EDEN's calm, analytical tone was a stark, jarring contrast to the raw emotion of the moment.
Noah looked up, and his expression, already grim, became even graver. Above the silent, burning city, the white flames began to flicker, to coalesce.
Horrifically, illusory scenes, replays of the carnage that had just unfolded, began to play out like a ghostly, silent film.
They saw it all again. The magnificent, desperate charge of the Royals and the Honored. The Justiciar's casual, brutal negation of their power.
The quiet, sickening crunch of the diamond golem. The dimming of the lightning Elemental's light. The silent, blossoming flower of white flame that had erased a thousand beings from existence.
It was a montage of absolute, pitiless slaughter, playing on a loop for all of existence to see.
|This only further affirms the conclusion, Master.|
|This action was meant to evoke strong emotions. The harvest of Emotive authority mixed with Everythings was the primary objective.|
|This public display... it is meant to evoke fear for all those who come after.|
Those who come after.
The words were a chilling premonition. And not long after RUIN/EDEN spoke them, they began to arrive!
Portals of ice and fire, of stone and storm, ripped open across the void.
Dukes of Living Elementals, their forms blazing with a furious, disbelieving light, appeared.

Behind them, legions of Royal and Honored Elementals materialized, their numbers in the tens of thousands. They saw the burning pyre that had been their home, and a collective, soul-shattering roar of grief and rage echoed through the silent Fold.
A few of the Dukes, their faces ashen masks of fury, shot towards Noah and Khor, the only other beings present in this graveyard.
"What happened here?!" one of them, a being of pure, molten obsidian, demanded, his accusatory glare a physical force.
Noah looked at them, at their paltry 100 Trillion in Complexity, and he felt... nothing.
A glimmer of his Haki, a faint, almost thoughtless pulse of his tyrannical will, washed over them.
They faltered, a sudden, suffocating pressure crushing their rage, their very authority groaning under a weight they could not comprehend.
"Can you not see in the flames?" Noah asked, his voice a cold, dead calm. "The one who did this did not hide. They made it perfectly clear."
The Elementals paled, their fury momentarily forgotten in the face of this new, oppressive power.
They turned their gazes to the burning city, to the silent, ghostly replay of the massacre, and they watched in a new, horrified silence.
Soon, others arrived. Living Temporals, their forms flickering with the echoes of a tragedy they were too late to prevent.
Living Quantums, who saw not just the destruction, but the million potential futures that had just been extinguished.

Living Origins, who looked upon this scene of absolute erasure with a profound, instinctual revulsion. The space around the burning citadel became a silent, somber congregation of the powerful beings in the Folds.
A Living Elemental Duke, a woman whose form was carved from a single, flawless glacier, her eyes burning with a cold, blue fire, roared.
She rose above the white flames, her hands raised to the void.
"DWINDLE!" she bellowed.
A torrent of glacial waves, a river of absolute-zero ice that could have frozen a star, cascaded down, seeking to snuff out the white flames.
But horrifically, the moment the ice touched the fire...
BOOM!
Tongues of white flame lashed out, not with heat, but with a pure, conceptual hunger.
They consumed the ice, the cold, the very authority of the attack. The glacial waves were swallowed like nothing, and the flames, now brighter, more arrogant, smashed into the Duke.
She was flung back, her form a screaming comet of shattered ice, a massive, gaping hole torn through her chest.
HUUM!
A chilling, absolute dread permeated the assembled crowd. The Duke, her entire front scorched by a fire that did not burn, roared, her voice now a screech of pure, unadulterated terror and fury.
"Call in an Emergency Kleos Concordat! Call it in! CALL IT IN!"
Her voice was a catalyst. A decision. The Living Existences had to understand what had happened here!
They had to prepare.
As Noah watched this new wave of chaos unfold, he received a new set of prompts from RUIN/EDEN, a quiet, analytical report in the midst of the storm.

|I have scanned all known facets of existence for any matching signatures or similarities.|

The Earliest Folds. The path forward was, once again, a descent into the past!

sentences.text: The white flames were a silent, terrible scream.
They did not roar or crackle; they burned with a profound, absolute quiet that was more unnerving than any sound!
Aeternitas Glacies, once a magnificent citadel of crystalline beauty, a monument to the serene, ordered power of the Living Elementals, was now a funeral pyre the size of a portion of the Folds.
The flames consumed everything...the shattered ice, the powdered diamond, the very memory of the lives that had been extinguished...and left nothing but a clean, sterile, and unending whiteness.
Prompts buzzed in his mind.
|Master, the post-event analysis of the Quantum Relocation Protocol is complete.|
|The Justiciar's descent was faster and slow.
The window for intervention was 1.7 nanoseconds.|
|Results of the emergency evacuation:|
| - Transcendent Wheels of Existence successfully relocated to a secure location in this Fold: 37 out of 37.|
| - Living Elementals (All Tiers) forcefully transported to the periphery of the blast zone: 30%.|
| - The 5 Dukes of Aeternitas Glacies were warned 0.8 nanoseconds prior to impact.
Their decision was to stand and fight.|
|Analysis: A tragic, yet statistically significant, success.
We have preserved a seed of their civilization that would have otherwise been completely erased.|
The silence was heavy
Noah and Khor floated in the void, silent witnesses to the aftermath.
The sheer, brutal efficiency of the slaughter, the absolute, unyielding nature of the Justiciar's power, had left a heavy, chilling silence between them.
"My current power cannot take that thing down," Khor finally said, her voice a low, flat statement of fact.
It was a rare, almost shocking admission of weakness from a being who had once devoured impossibilities for breakfast.
Noah nodded, his gaze fixed on the burning city.
"Have you seen anything like it before?"
Khor was silent for a long moment, her abyssal eyes lost in the depths of her fragmented memories.
"Maybe," she whispered, the word a fragile, uncertain thing.
"In the Earliest Folds...
I remember the memories of some of the Inevitabilities.
They showed... a certain Tribe of Early Creatures.
They were builders, artisans of destruction.
They made things like that.
But the memories are scattered, broken."
Her form trembled, not with fear, but with a rage that was so cold it threatened to freeze the very space around them.
"I am going to kill every last one of them, Outsider," she hissed, her voice a venomous promise.
"All those who aided in doing this to the Inevitabilities.
THE Living Paradox... all of them."
The silence that followed her vow was heavy, absolute, and filled with the promise of a future reckoning.
And then, a new, chilling voice cut through the quiet.
|Master.|
RUIN/EDEN's calm, analytical tone was a stark, jarring contrast to the raw emotion of the moment.
Noah looked up, and his expression, already grim, became even graver.
Above the silent, burning city, the white flames began to flicker, to coalesce.
Horrifically, illusory scenes, replays of the carnage that had just unfolded, began to play out like a ghostly, silent film.
They saw it all again.
The magnificent, desperate charge of the Royals and the Honored.
The Justiciar's casual, brutal negation of their power.
The quiet, sickening crunch of the diamond golem.
The dimming of the lightning Elemental's light.
The silent, blossoming flower of white flame that had erased a thousand beings from existence.
It was a montage of absolute, pitiless slaughter, playing on a loop for all of existence to see.
|This only further affirms the conclusion, Master.|
|This action was meant to evoke strong emotions.
The harvest of Emotive authority mixed with Everythings was the primary objective.|
|This public display... it is meant to evoke fear for all those who come after.|
Those who come after.
The words were a chilling premonition.
And not long after RUIN/EDEN spoke them, they began to arrive!
Portals of ice and fire, of stone and storm, ripped open across the void.
Dukes of Living Elementals, their forms blazing with a furious, disbelieving light, appeared.
Behind them, legions of Royal and Honored Elementals materialized, their numbers in the tens of thousands.
They saw the burning pyre that had been their home, and a collective, soul-shattering roar of grief and rage echoed through the silent Fold.
A few of the Dukes, their faces ashen masks of fury, shot towards Noah and Khor, the only other beings present in this graveyard.
"What happened here?!" one of them, a being of pure, molten obsidian, demanded, his accusatory glare a physical force.
Noah looked at them, at their paltry 100 Trillion in Complexity, and he felt... nothing.
A glimmer of his Haki, a faint, almost thoughtless pulse of his tyrannical will, washed over them.
They faltered, a sudden, suffocating pressure crushing their rage, their very authority groaning under a weight they could not comprehend.
"Can you not see in the flames?" Noah asked, his voice a cold, dead calm.
"The one who did this did not hide.
They made it perfectly clear."
The Elementals paled, their fury momentarily forgotten in the face of this new, oppressive power.
They turned their gazes to the burning city, to the silent, ghostly replay of the massacre, and they watched in a new, horrified silence.
Soon, others arrived.
Living Temporals, their forms flickering with the echoes of a tragedy they were too late to prevent.
Living Quantums, who saw not just the destruction, but the million potential futures that had just been extinguished.
Living Origins, who looked upon this scene of absolute erasure with a profound, instinctual revulsion.
The space around the burning citadel became a silent, somber congregation of the powerful beings in the Folds.
A Living Elemental Duke, a woman whose form was carved from a single, flawless glacier, her eyes burning with a cold, blue fire, roared.
She rose above the white flames, her hands raised to the void.
"DWINDLE!" she bellowed.
A torrent of glacial waves, a river of absolute-zero ice that could have frozen a star, cascaded down, seeking to snuff out the white flames.
But horrifically, the moment the ice touched the fire...
BOOM!
Tongues of white flame lashed out, not with heat, but with a pure, conceptual hunger.
They consumed the ice, the cold, the very authority of the attack.
The glacial waves were swallowed like nothing, and the flames, now brighter, more arrogant, smashed into the Duke.
She was flung back, her form a screaming comet of shattered ice, a massive, gaping hole torn through her chest.
HUUM!
A chilling, absolute dread permeated the assembled crowd.
The Duke, her entire front scorched by a fire that did not burn, roared, her voice now a screech of pure, unadulterated terror and fury.
"Call in an Emergency Kleos Concordat!
Call it in!
CALL IT IN!"
Her voice was a catalyst.
A decision.
The Living Existences had to understand what had happened here!
They had to prepare.

chapters.title: Chapter 4253 The Early Laboratories! I
paragraphs: Among the many arriving to witness the devastation, Noah saw them.
The Living Emotives. Their faces showed immense sorrow, their auras radiating a grief so profound it seemed to amplify the tragedy of the scene.
His eyes flashed with suspicion. He sent a silent command to RUIN/EDEN.
'Keep a closer eye on the Transcendent Emotive Folds from now on.'
|Confirmed, Master. Continuous, deep-level surveillance has been initiated.|
|Hypothesis: There are significant gaps in our current knowledge regarding the motivations of the entities within THE Loom.|

|It is possible that the Justiciar's secondary objective of inducing fear and harvesting Emotive authority was a directive added by THE Living Emotive for their own purposes, separate from the primary function of the Lodestone failsafe.|
|The mentalities and intricacies of Level One Scale existences are, by their very nature, complex and often contradictory. More data is required to form a complete picture.|

Yes. Those in THE Loom gained nothing from this public display of terror. All the Justiciar had seemed to collect were Everythings saturated with the authority of Emotive. The why of it all... the answer had to be in the Earliest Folds.
"Collect more data here," Noah murmured, his voice a low command to RUIN/EDEN. "Note how the Living Emotives react. For now... let us get some answers."
|Yes, Master.|
Back in the Early Veiled Shore, Noah's main body stood on the golden sands, the quiet, purposeful hum of his domain a soothing balm on his turbulent thoughts.
He needed to be stronger. He needed to be faster. He needed to be ready for whatever came next.
|Master, the subject Infiniverse has completed the forging of forty new Seed Glyphs of Perpetual Harvest. The endowments are ready for distribution at your command.|
He nodded. "Proceed."
A new storm of verdant-gold light, a hurricane of pure, conceptual growth, descended upon the Shore.
Forty endowments, each one a testament to the impossible, recursive power of his Principle, washed over him as all were used for him!
When the storm passed, he felt... denser. More real. His power, already measured in the dozens of Quadrillions, had taken another leap.
Khor floated beside him, her expression now a mask of grim resolve. "I will go back with you," she said, her voice a quiet, unshakeable promise. "Even if I am just a voice in your head, I will help."
Noah nodded, then turned his gaze to the pulsating, crimson-blue cluster of infinity symbols that was his new system.
"RUIN/EDEN, how close are you to grasping the Cultivation of Everythings?"
|Analysis is ongoing, Master. The methodology is complex. I have not yet reached a point of practical application.|
He had expected as much.
For now, he had to use the tools he possessed.
He looked over at Sigrid, at his Mother, at Moiraine, and everyone else here who was acclimating to their own existence.
He looked towards The Infiniverse who nodded her head as she had much to do.
He then...closed his eyes, his will reaching into the very heart of his being, to the star-chart of his Early Atlas of the Folds.

The other part of his body that was Ozymandias was already contained in the depths of his existence, and he would unleash it for potentially more opportunities as needed to make sure he could stay in the Earliest Folds as long as possible.
With all preparations ready...
He activated it.
|Temporal Traversal Initiated.|
|Analysis: The unique signature and weavings of the Justiciar have been cross-referenced with all accessible temporal data points within the Atlas.|
|A match has been found. The weavings correspond to three potential locations within the Earliest Folds.|
|Due to the complete advancement of all 159 Towers of Osmont to the Vital Lighthouse stage, and the current strength of your Heart, a precise destination can now be selected.|
|Destination Locked: The Early Laboratories.|
A column of pure, temporal light, a river of a billion frozen moments, descended and enveloped his form.
The traversal was different this time. Smoother. More stable. The violent, chaotic journey of his earlier trips had been replaced by a serene, controlled descent through the layers of time.
His Vital Lighthouses were not just anchors; they were a navigation system, a perfect, celestial GPS guiding him through the storm!
|Traversal is stable. Estimated duration in the Earliest Folds: 7 Days.|
HUUM!
Not hours, not a day, but 7 days!
He could stay in the Earliest Folds for 7 days!
The process...was unfathomably quicker this time around.
The light faded, and he arrived after what seemed like mere seconds.
WU!
He stood in a grand, open-air location, surrounded by massive, monolithic white stones that were arranged in a complex, concentric pattern.
He was at the very center, on a raised platform forged from a seamless fusion of stone, wood, and a strange, dark metal that seemed to absorb the ambient light.
The air was clean, sterile, and hummed with a quiet, intellectual energy.
|Welcome to The Early Laboratories.|
|Scanning of nearby areas has begun.|
|Preliminary scans show multiple Early Creatures gazing directly at you.|
Noah's gaze swept across the stone-henge-like area.
At the edges, standing silently between the great white stones, were nine figures.
Nine Early Creatures, their forms perfect and powerful, staring back at him!
All of them were adorned in simple, elegant white chiton robes.
RUIN/EDEN's analysis flashed in his vision, a cascade of names and terrifying numbers.
[Lyra - 50 Quadrillion Complexity, 50 Quadrillion Purity]
[Orion - 80 Quadrillion Complexity, 80 Quadrillion Purity]
[Cassiopeia - 120 Quadrillion Complexity, 120 Quadrillion Purity]
[Cepheus - 400 Quadrillion Complexity, 400 Quadrillion Purity]
None of them showed hostility.
Their gazes were calm, curious, and unnervingly analytical, as if they were scientists observing a fascinating new specimen.
In that tense, silent moment, a new voice echoed out from a distant, unseen location, a voice filled with a terrifying, impatient power.
"What are you all doing? Bring the newcomer that has been sent over!"
The voice was a thunderclap of authority, a command that made the very stones of the laboratory hum.
Noah's eyes opened wide as the frequency of this voice was unique.
And it was a voice that, shockingly, did not belong to an Early Creature.
It felt like the voice of...a Fold Dweller!
And yet, it was commanding Early Creatures!

chapters.title: Chapter 4254 The Early Laboratories! II
paragraphs: The command was a thunderclap in the serene, intellectual quiet of the Laboratories.
It was a voice that did not ask, but simply was, a fundamental law of this strange, sterile place!
The nine Early Creatures, beings of such immense power that they could have unmade Folds with a thought, did not flinch. They simply... obeyed.
Cepheus, the four-hundred-quadrillion-complexity giant whose gaze had been the most intense, turned his ancient, starlit eyes to Noah.
He beckoned, a simple, almost casual gesture. "We were not expecting another Assistant to be sent over so soon," he said, his voice the low, rumbling sound of distant Wheels colliding.
"Where did THE Living Concept find you in such short notice? I thought another Elderborn would not be found so quickly."
BOOM!
THE Living Concept!
Elderborn!
Terrifying words echoed out as Noah's mind buzzed, with his entrance this time around actually being into an environment where the Weavings of THE Living Concept were taking place!
And Elderborn.
The term was a key, a clue, a new variable in an equation that was growing more complex by the second.
Noah's eyes flashed with a sharp, analytical light, but he tilted his head, his expression a perfect mask of polite, well-meaning ignorance.
"What do you mean, Elderborn?"
At his question, the nine Early Creatures looked at each other, and a sound that had likely not been heard in this place for eons rippled through the air: laughter.
It was not a sound of mirth, but a dry, academic chuckle, the sound of those who knew more amused by a student's fundamental, yet understandable, lack of knowledge.
"Ah, of course," another of the Creatures, Lyra, said, her voice a melody of pure, mathematical harmony.
"THE Living Concept has a tendency to... omit the introductory materials. It believes in learning through immersion, I suppose."
Cepheus gestured for Noah to walk with them, and the group began to move deeper into the stone-henge-like structure.

"An Elderborn," he explained, his tone now that of a patient, if somewhat condescending, mentor, "is an existence with a high concentration of the Everythings of THE Creature. Our own existences are born from the weavings of the Folds and THE Creature, shaped by the authorities of THE Living Existences. But you...and others are different. Your very essence carries a significant, foundational echo of the First Cause. You have qualities others do not, and are able to interact with existence in ways others cannot. It is why you are helpful to the research of THE Living Concept."
HUUM!
The shocking information was delivered with the casual air of a tour guide explaining a local landmark.
As they walked, Noah's internal world was a flurry of activity.
|New Data Point Acquired: [Elderborn].|
|Definition: An existence possessing a high concentration of the Everythings of [THE Creature].|

|Analysis: This is a significant variable. It is the reason why they believe you were 'sent' here. More information required for you to play thr part. Recommend continued feigned ignorance to maximize data acquisition.|
Noah nodded internally, his outward expression remaining one of polite curiosity.
'Khor,' his thoughts were a silent whisper, 'have you heard this term before?'
Her voice, a familiar, ancient echo in his mind, was calm.

'I knew of some, like The First Leader, Gilgamesh, who were known to have high concentrations of Everythings. But I did not bother to know all the terms others were called by. And these so-called Elderborns may be different from those like The First Leader. Be cautious, Outsider.'
As they moved past the rising stones, the landscape opened up.
The same white material of the floor continued in a neat, perfect grid, and from it, massive white walls rose all around.
They were arranged in a series of disconnected, circular clusters, creating a labyrinth of sterile, white canyons.
And the deeper they went, the more terrifying the air felt, thick with a power so dense and so ancient it made his own existence feel... new.
Another of the Early Creatures, a being of pure, shifting light named Orion, turned to him with a grin that was all predatory intellect.
"Just because you are an Elderborn does not mean you are in for a grand opportunity," he said, his voice a crackle of static and starlight.

"There have been multiple Elderborns who were simply not up to par. We have had to collapse all their memories of this place before sending them away. Who knows... you may just be one of those... Bahaha!"
At his mocking laughter, the sharp, impatient voice that had summoned them echoed out again, this time much closer, its authority cutting through the air like a blade.
"Do not scare the newcomer before they have even been tested. You all can go back now. You... come forward."

They had entered a clearing, a vast, circular space at the heart of the labyrinth. The white walls here were surrounded by a single, colossal structure made of a strange, crystalline glass that seemed to absorb and refract the ambient light in impossible ways.
And standing before it was the source of the voice.
She was...a Fold Dweller.
A being of impossible, breathtaking beauty. Her hair was a cascade of stellar, dark silk, and her eyes held the cold, brilliant light of a distant quasar.
Her body was adorned in a simple white chiton that hugged a figure of perfect, dangerous grace.
|[Commander Elara]|
|Classification: Prime Fold Dweller|
The Early Creatures harrumphed at being bossed around by a being who was not one of them, but they listened.
They began to move back, their task complete. But before they could go too far, the Fold Dweller's gaze swept over Noah, a quick, dismissive up-and-down assessment.
"Oh," she said, her voice a whip-crack of command, "go to Sector 9-D and bring out the defective Elderborn who wasn't able to react with anything. Treat him with the same procedures."
A defeective Elderborn that wss not able to react with anything!
Noah noted all of this down as he went forward!
